can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of common adjectives.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: add another brushstroke

positives: The car is big and beautiful.
The food is hot and good.
negatives: are the ASTM and OSHA.
This is an overdimension and overweight.

can_do_statement: Can use 'very' with a limited range of common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: very pushes the attribute up the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: turn it up

positives: The house is very big.
This book is very good.
negatives: They are very rural.
It is very efficiency.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives attributively, before a noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: determiner + adjective + noun — slot the adjective before its noun as a foreground modifier
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker foregrounds a property directly on the entity

positives: I have a big house.
He bought a new car.
negatives: A difficult English is hard to learn.
A little better or slow?

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives predicatively, after 'be'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: be then the word

negatives: My bedroom is a mess.
This place is the best.
She was singing loudly.
positives: My bedroom is big.
This place is lovely.

can_do_statement: Can use the irregular superlative adjective 'best' in the phrase 'my best friend'.

ontology.mental_model: one person crowned as top member of a set by the speaker
ontology.pedagogical_hook: crown your number-one person
ontology.agency_or_distance: possessive anchors the ranking to the speaker's own world

positives: She's my best friend.
Marco has been my best friend since primary school.
negatives: I always try to do my best.
This is the best pizza in town.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'soon' in the phrases 'See you soon' and 'Get well soon', as a signing-off device.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: see you / get well + soon — closes the conversation with a forward-pointing adverb
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker hands the hearer a near-future expectation as a parting signal

positives: See you soon!
Get well soon.
negatives: I will see you soon.
We'll see you soon.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('here', 'there') to indicate place.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: here / there — point to a place on the conversational stage
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker deictically anchors an entity in shared space

positives: I use my headphones here to concentrate.
I live there now.
negatives: There are other conversations in English.
There was a factory near my town.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'really' and 'very much' with verbs expressing preference ('like', 'love'), for emphasis.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: really / very much + like/love — turn the dial past the standard setting
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks the affective state as more than ordinary

positives: I really like pizza.
She really loves cats.
negatives: It's really like an idle month.
Really like a tutor.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'very' to make adjectives stronger.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: very + adjective — push the adjective past its default setting
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker escalates the force of a quality word

positives: Keep practicing because some text is very difficult.
It is very interesting when you explain.
negatives: They are very rural.
I need something very efficiency.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('always', 'sometimes') to talk about frequency.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: always / sometimes — place the event on a frequency dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the event on the spectrum from never-to-always

positives: I always wake up early.
They sometimes go there.
negatives: Sometimes is more related to other things.
Sometimes are two main reasons.

can_do_statement: Can use 'very' to modify common gradable adjectives.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'very' before words like 'good' or 'nice' to make them stronger.

positives: My home is very nice.
My teacher is very good.
negatives: She ran very fast.
Thank you very much.

can_do_statement: Can use 'very' to modify time adverbs. ► adverb phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'very soon' or 'very early' to show something happens at an extreme time.

positives: I hope you get well very soon.
I have a lesson very early.
negatives: She is very nice.
We arrived at the very end.

can_do_statement: Can use place adverbs ('here', 'there') as complements of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Situating an entity in a spatial location
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'here' or 'there' right after verbs like 'be' or 'go'.

positives: I am happy here because people are very nice.
You must go there.
negatives: There are many people in the room.
Here is your pen.

guideword: FORM: DEGREE and TIME, MODIFYING VERBS
can_do_statement: Can use degree and time adverbs to modify verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Modifying the frequency or intensity of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Put words like 'always', 'sometimes', or 'really' right before the verb.

positives: I really like Japanese music.
I always go to the park with my children.
negatives: It is a really good book.
She is always happy.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs in front position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Sometimes / Often / Yesterday / Tomorrow — slot the adverb at the head of the clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker opens the clause with a framing adverb

positives: Sometimes I go to the beach.
Tomorrow I will see her at the airport.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She finished her homework.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs before an adjective.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: very / really / quite + adjective — slot the intensifier just before the adjective
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker intensifies the adjective from a zero position

positives: It is really good.
She is so nice.
negatives: I really don't want to go.
So for English class I study.

can_do_statement: Can use frequency adverbs in the usual mid position, between the subject and the main verb.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + always/usually/often/sometimes + verb — slot the adverb between subject and verb
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks the verb's frequency medially

positives: I always wake up early.
She never eats meat.
negatives: Sometimes I go to the park.
I am always tired.

can_do_statement: Can use 'really' in the usual mid-position, between the subject and the main verb.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + really + verb — slot the intensifier between subject and main verb

positives: I really like this book.
She really wants a dog.
negatives: This is really good.
I am really tired.

can_do_statement: Can use time adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + yesterday/today/tomorrow/soon/now/just/already — anchor the time at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker places the time at the end of the clause

positives: I hope to see you soon.
She went to the park yesterday.
negatives: I went to the bank.
She finished her homework.

can_do_statement: Can use place adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + here/there/nearby/abroad/away/upstairs/downstairs — anchor the place at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates entities at the end of the clause

positives: I want to go there.
We are eating outside.
negatives: There is a dog.
We went outside the house.

can_do_statement: Can modify adverbs of time and degree with 'very'.

ontology.mental_model: Scaling temporal or degree adverbs to high intensity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Modifying simple adverbs of time and degree with 'very'

positives: I hope you will be fine very soon.
I like my job very much.
negatives: It is very good.
He is very tall.

can_do_statement: Can omit the subject in a second main declarative clause when the subject is obvious or the same as the first clause.

ontology.mental_model: Linking actions to the same subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying what you do without repeating 'I'

positives: She likes to listen to music and watch TV.
Sometimes I go to the park and play tennis.
negatives: I went home and he stayed.
She likes music and TV.

can_do_statement: Can combine two main declarative clauses using co-ordinating conjunctions ('and', 'but', 'or').

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Connecting sentences with basic conjunctions

positives: I like my college and I like my class.
I visit my friends, but I often stay at home.
negatives: I like apples and oranges.
She is tall and beautiful.

can_do_statement: Can form simple affirmative declarative clauses.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Making simple statements

positives: I study English at college.
My friend is a nurse.
negatives: Are you my friend?
Go to the store.

can_do_statement: Can form a simple negative declarative clause with lexical 'be' + 'not' or 'n't'.

ontology.mental_model: Stating that an entity lacks a certain attribute or identity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negative state of being

positives: My college is not very big.
This place isn't big.
negatives: He isn't going to the store.
I haven't got any time.

can_do_statement: Can form simple negative declarative clauses.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Simple negation of actions

positives: I don't like maths.
He doesn't know.
negatives: I am not happy.
I haven't seen it.

guideword: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE DECLARATIVE, MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
can_do_statement: Can form an affirmative declarative clause with modal verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing ability, permission, or future intent
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic modal usage

positives: I can go to see her tomorrow.
I will visit you soon.
negatives: Can I go?
I cannot see you.

can_do_statement: Can form interrogative clauses with 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about entity state or identity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Questions with the verb 'to be'

positives: How are you?
Are you ok?
negatives: I am ok.
He is happy.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with 'because', after a main clause, to introduce reasons.

ontology.mental_model: Explaining the cause of a state or action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'because' in the middle of a sentence to provide a reason for the main clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Connecting an outcome directly to its originating cause

positives: I love her because she is friendly.
I like my television because it is big.
negatives: Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
Because of the rain, we left.

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine phrases.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring parallel parts of speech or phrases into a unified communicative whole.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use simple linkers to connect related phrases side-by-side.

positives: The kitchen is quite large and brightly lit.
She likes to go to the cinema or to the theatre.
negatives: And I went home.
He came in and sat down.

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine sentences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a new sentence with 'And', 'But', or 'Or' to carry forward the previous idea.

positives: He is very clever. But he never studies.
And then we went to the market.
negatives: I like apples and oranges.
They can either stay here or go home.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' and 'or' before the final item in a list.

ontology.mental_model: Organizing sequential items before concluding a list.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a comma for the first items, and save the linker for the very last item.

positives: I bought milk, bread, and cheese.
We can visit Paris, Rome, or Madrid.
negatives: He sings and dances.
I don't know if he came or went.

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to combine clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Integrating distinct actions or states into a single complex sentence.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use these words to glue two complete mini-sentences together.

positives: He is a doctor, and he works very hard.
She didn't like the food, but she ate it anyway.
negatives: I want a burger and fries.
The tall but ugly building.

can_do_statement: Can use single word conjunctions ('and, but, or') to connect single nouns and adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: Pairing basic vocabulary words directly together.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Connect two nouns or two adjectives simply with 'and', 'but', or 'or'.

positives: The cat is black and white.
Do you want tea or coffee?
negatives: He came in and sat down.
And I agree with you.

can_do_statement: Can use 'but' to add an unexpected contrast.

ontology.mental_model: Introducing a contrastive or unexpected element.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'but' to signal a twist or an unexpected consequence.

positives: It was raining, but we still went out.
The car is old but reliable.
negatives: I want apples and oranges.
He is tall, so he plays basketball.

can_do_statement: Can use 'because' as a subordinating conjunction to introduce a subordinate clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: reason clause

positives: I want a big garden because I have children.
She likes meeting other people because she wants to improve her English.
negatives: Because of the rain, we stayed inside.
I did it just because of you.

can_do_statement: Can use articles 'the', 'a' and 'an' before nouns. ► noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: articles with nouns

positives: She lives in a flat.
I have an appointment.
negatives: It is a very good place.
It is an old house.

can_do_statement: Can use 'a' + 'very' + adjectives in basic noun phrases. ► adverbs ►  noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: a very + adjective

positives: He's a very good man.
It is a very beautiful place.
negatives: I am very happy.
She has a very.

can_do_statement: Can use 'a' and 'an' before adjectives in a noun phrase. ► adjectives ►  noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: article + adjective

positives: You can make a quick snack.
It is an interesting place.
negatives: He's a very good man.
I have an appointment.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the' in prepositional phrases relating to time.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: preposition + the + noun of time

positives: I work at the weekend and I'm very busy.
I can come to see you on Friday in the morning.
negatives: I live in the city.
I saw it on the table.

can_do_statement: Can use no article before a limited range of nouns in some fixed expressions with prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Spatial and conceptual relationships formalized without specific entity bounding.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Common prepositional phrases lack articles because they treat locations or times as concepts.

positives: I am at home right now.
We usually travel by bus.
negatives: I am at the home of my friend.
Look at that car.

can_do_statement: Can use no article before a limited range of singular, plural and uncountable nouns when referring to things in general.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using no article for general activities or uncountable materials.

positives: In my free time I usually play football.
I really like rice and sweet dishes.
negatives: I threw the football to him.
The rice is burning.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in a limited range of contexts to refer to places from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific place or thing.

positives: I love living in this city.
This area is very nice.
negatives: I like this book.
This is a big house.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with time and date words to refer to 'the one that's coming'.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of future temporal points or periods.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'this' upcoming event or time.

positives: This summer I want to go on holiday.
I have a good plan for this weekend.
negatives: Last summer was great.
I will go next weekend.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with singular nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item.

positives: I like this place because it is very nice.
If you like, then we can go this Saturday.
negatives: I like that place.
I like these places.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiners 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her' and 'our' before nouns. ► noun phrases ► possessive pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: I live with my family.
She lost her favorite book.
negatives: He is looking at me.
I saw them yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('some', 'lots of', 'a lot of' and numbers).

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: Near my home there are some shops.
My house has got three rooms.
negatives: I have a lot of water.
There is some trouble here.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('a', 'every').► determiners: articles

ontology.mental_model: Singling out a specific countable entity or referring to all instances distributively.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a' for one thing or 'every' for all things of that type.

positives: I go to college every day.
I have a big kitchen in my house.
negatives: I go to college all days.
I have big kitchens in my house.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative forms 'will' and ''ll'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' to talk about the future in affirmative sentences.

positives: I will see you soon.
They'll come at seven.
negatives: I will not do it.
He left a will for his children.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' and ''ll' to talk about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' to express personal plans and intentions.

positives: I will try to come tomorrow.
We'll bring a football with us.
negatives: It will rain tomorrow.
The sun will rise at six.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker asserts capability, permission, or possibility using the modal 'can' with a verb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'can' followed by a base verb to talk about things we are able or allowed to do.

positives: You can see a lot of special places.
We can make a quick snack.
negatives: I cannot come to see you.
Can you come for dinner?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative question form.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker requests permission, information, or action by moving 'can' before the subject.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To make a question, start with 'Can' then add the person and the verb.

positives: Can you come for dinner Monday?
Can we go to the park?
negatives: You can come for dinner.
I cannot see you today.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker asserts lack of capability or permission using 'cannot' or 'can't'.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'cannot' or 'can't' to say something is not possible or not allowed.

positives: I cannot come to see you.
I can't say anything.
negatives: I can cook.
Can you come on Sunday?

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' to make an offer.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker offers assistance or an action using 'can I' or 'I can' with specific offer verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'Can I help you?' or 'I can do it' to kindly offer our help to someone.

positives: Can I help you with that?
I can bring some food if you want.
negatives: He can help us.
Can you help me?

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' to talk about ability to do something.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker describes an innate or learned physical or mental capability using ability verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'can' to talk about things you know how to do, like 'I can swim' or 'I can cook'.

positives: I can cook very well.
She can't read this language.
negatives: Can I help you?
You can leave now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' to make a request.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker attempts to direct the listener to perform an action using a 'can you' question.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask someone to do something for you, start your question with 'Can you...'.

positives: Can you come on Sunday?
Can you call me later?
negatives: You can wear anything.
Can I help you?

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' to talk about possibility.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker outlines what is factually or circumstantially possible using circumstantial verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'can' to talk about things that are possible in a certain place or situation.

positives: There you can find milk and juice.
I cannot see you today.
negatives: I can cook dinner.
Can you come on Sunday?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Future statements

positives: I will be at your house at 7.30.
I'll come to see you tomorrow morning.
negatives: Will you come?
I will not be there.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to talk about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Future intentions

positives: I will bring some music to the dinner.
We'll see you tomorrow.
negatives: Will you come with me?
I won't be there.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would like to invite' to make invitations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would like to invite' for formal offers

positives: I would like to invite you to dinner.
We'd like to invite them to our house.
negatives: I invited him to dinner last night.
I would like a coffee right now.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'like'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would like' for polite wishes

positives: I would like some tea.
He'd like to go to the park.
negatives: I would not like that very much.
She wouldn't like it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would like' to talk about wishes and preferences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would like to [verb]' for preferences

positives: I would like to travel the world.
I'd like to eat chicken.
negatives: I would like a coffee.
I like to travel the world.

can_do_statement: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the present simple with 'don't' + main verb. ► present simple ► can

ontology.mental_model: Negating actions in the present simple.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'don't' before a main verb to form a negative statement.

positives: I don't have a dining room.
We don't like other lessons.
negatives: I didn't have a dining room.
Do you like lessons?

can_do_statement: Can form negative statements of main verb 'be', with contracted and uncontracted forms.

ontology.mental_model: Negating states or identities in the present.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'am not', 'isn't', 'aren't' for negative statements.

positives: My college is not very big.
I'm not a good swimmer.
negatives: I am not swimming today.
The cake was not eaten.

can_do_statement: Can use negative form 'can’t'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'can't' for things you are unable or not allowed to do.

positives: In winter, we can't go visiting because it is too cold.
I can not find my CD.
negatives: You can go if you want to.
Canning fruits is a fun activity, not boring.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying plural nouns with an adjective and no determiner.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using adjective plus plural noun without a/the

positives: I have new neighbours.
I like reading interesting books in the Library.
negatives: I have some new neighbours.
The nice people waved at us.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying singular and plural nouns with an adjective after a determiner.

ontology.mental_model: Attaching a property to an entity that has been identified
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a descriptive word right before the thing you are talking about, after pointing it out.

positives: I have a big garden.
She loves her new car.
negatives: The car is big.
A garden can be big.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + singular and plural nouns. ► Nouns and noun phrases: functions

ontology.mental_model: Identifying or singling out a specific entity or quantity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using pointer words like 'a', 'the', 'my', or 'this' before a noun.

positives: I like this place.
My husband is a teacher.
negatives: She walked quickly.
They are very beautiful.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases by pre-modifying a limited range of nouns with another noun.

ontology.mental_model: Combining two entities to create a more specific category of the second entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a noun like an adjective to describe another noun.

positives: I like to play computer games.
She makes excellent tomato sauce.
negatives: I have a fast computer.
Tomatoes are delicious.

can_do_statement: Can use proper nouns with a capital letter to refer to specific people, places, days and things.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Capitalized specific names of people, places, or days.

positives: I went to London.
My friend is Monika.
negatives: Sunday is a good day.
Cars are fast.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of common nouns.

ontology.mental_model: General categories of objects, people, or concepts
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic common nouns for everyday things.

positives: My house is big.
I read a book.
negatives: Water the plants.
I will book a flight.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of compound nouns, as one-word, two-word and hyphenated compounds, formed from verb + noun, noun + noun and adjective + noun combinations.

ontology.mental_model: Two concepts fused into a single new entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Nouns made up of two or more words acting as a single unit.

positives: I went to the swimming pool.
Wait at the bus stop.
negatives: I was swimming in the lake.
The bus is late.

can_do_statement: Can form plurals by adding '-s' to common countable nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic regular plural nouns ending in s.

positives: We play computer games.
I have three books.
negatives: He plays football.
The dog barks.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as subjects of the clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a noun or noun phrase at the beginning of a clause as its subject.

positives: His name is Stanislav.
My friends are from Poland.
negatives: It is raining today.
There are three apples.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of prepositions in prepositional phrases.

ontology.mental_model: Objects connected by spatial, temporal, or logical relations
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using nouns after prepositions like 'in', 'on', 'at'.

positives: I like everything in my house.
He is waiting for dinner.
negatives: I want to go.
He walked in.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as objects of the clause.

ontology.mental_model: Nouns acting as receivers of actions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using nouns directly after verbs as objects.

positives: I love my house.
I visit my family.
negatives: I am tired.
She smiled brightly.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as adjuncts in some time expressions.

ontology.mental_model: Nouns acting as temporal setting for events
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Time phrases using nouns without prepositions.

positives: I will see you tomorrow morning.
I will write to you again next week.
negatives: He is the next person.
This is a good book.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of the verb 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: Noun equates to the subject via the copula
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using nouns after 'be' to describe who or what someone is.

positives: He is a student.
It is my house.
negatives: He is playing.
It is big.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple affirmative using regular or irregular verbs.

positives: I went to class at 9 am.
My grandmother lived in a village.
negatives: I go to class at 9 am.
My grandmother lives in a village.

can_do_statement: Can use the past simple to talk about everyday events or states.

ontology.mental_model: Everyday state or event completed in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using past simple for descriptions and recurring states.

positives: The people were very polite.
I liked this place very much.
negatives: The people are very polite.
I like this place very much.

can_do_statement: Can form prepositional phrases with a preposition and a noun phrase.

ontology.mental_model: Connecting objects, places or times to the main sentence.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use prepositions like 'in', 'on', or 'with' followed by a noun or noun phrase to add details.

positives: When I have free time, I go to the park with my dog.
We have lots of fruit in the summer.
negatives: I am happy.
She runs fast.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of simple (single-word) prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Basic relations between entities, locations, or times.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Common single words like 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to' connect places or times to the action.

positives: I'm sending some flowers to you.
He works in Bognor Regis.
negatives: I am happy.
She runs fast.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming the continuous aspect with a 'be' auxiliary and an '-ing' participle.

positives: I am sending you some beautiful flowers.
She is writing a long letter right now.
negatives: I am not playing tennis today.
He is a very good boy.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using fundamental dynamic verbs in the continuous aspect.

positives: I am sending you these pretty flowers.
We are doing more speaking now.
negatives: I am watching a fast swimming competition.
I made a big chocolate cake yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple negative basics

positives: I don't like meat and fish.
She doesn't know the place.
negatives: I do like meat.
They didn't know the answer.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple to talk about repeated events or habits, and general facts.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple for routines

positives: I work in a supermarket.
It takes 25 minutes by car.
negatives: I am working in a supermarket.
They worked hard yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Basic statements of fact or state
ontology.pedagogical_hook: First present simple verbs

positives: I learn new words every day.
She plays tennis at the weekend.
negatives: I learned a new word yesterday.
They are playing tennis right now.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with the adverb 'really' as an intensifier. ► adverbs

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple with 'really'

positives: I really like my new kitchen.
She really wants to see you.
negatives: I like my new kitchen very much.
He really wanted to go home.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronouns 'you' and 'it' after 'be' in question forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking basic questions

positives: How are you today?
Is it going to rain?
negatives: You are my best friend.
I think it is very good.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronoun 'it' as a direct object to refer to an object or situation already referred to.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'it' to avoid repetition

positives: I bought a new book and I love it.
She found it under the table.
negatives: It is a sunny day.
I think it will rain tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use the object pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'it', 'us' and 'them' in the object position after prepositions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Who or what the action is directed towards

positives: She gave the book to him.
I want to go with them.
negatives: He told me to go.
I saw him yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'we' and 'they' after an auxiliary or modal verb in question forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions with modal/aux

positives: Can we go now?
What do they want?
negatives: We can go now.
They do not want to go.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'us' and 'them' in the direct object position after a transitive verb.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Receiving the action of a verb

positives: I will call him later.
She told us a story.
negatives: He went to the store.
To him, it was perfect.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronoun 'it' before 'be' to refer to a first person speaker or writer.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying yourself on the phone or at a door

positives: Hello, it's me.
Hi John, it is Sarah.
negatives: It is cold outside.
It's raining now.

can_do_statement: Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we' and 'they' in the subject position before a verb in statements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Stating who does the action

positives: She plays tennis.
We are going home.
negatives: The cat runs fast.
John is a doctor.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of indefinite pronouns as objects.

ontology.mental_model: Referring to unspecified things or people as the recipient of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: basic indefinite pronoun as object

positives: I like doing everything at College.
I can clean your house and cook something for you.
negatives: Everything is going to be okay.
Something fell off the table.

can_do_statement: Can use 'everything' as subject, with a singular verb.

ontology.mental_model: Totalizing referent initiating an action or state
ontology.pedagogical_hook: everything + singular verb

positives: I hope everything is all right.
Everything looks nice and green there.
negatives: She knows everything about computers.
I told him everything I knew.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.  ► can

ontology.mental_model: Making simple requests or asking about basic abilities
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask yes/no questions using 'can' for ability or requests

positives: Can you come to dinner in my house?
I can't find my CD, can you bring some music please?
negatives: I can do it myself.
She asked if I can come over.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Verbs like 'listen' always take 'to' when indicating what is heard.

positives: I listen to music in the living room.
I can look after her if she needs.
negatives: I can look around the house today.
They asked me a quick question.

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary verb 'be'. ►  present continuous

ontology.pedagogical_hook: The 'be' verb helps mark the action as happening right now.

positives: I am writing to tell you what I do every day.
We are going to the park.
negatives: I am a good student.
They are happy today.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of modal auxiliary verbs ('can', 'will', 'would').

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using basic modals can, will, would

positives: Can you bring some music with you?
I'll be very happy to help you today.
negatives: I am able to bring some music.
She wants to be very happy.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verb 'be'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'be' as a main linking verb

positives: I am twenty years old.
It is a very nice apartment.
negatives: I am walking to the park.
The car was stolen last night.

can_do_statement: Can use regular and irregular main verbs in simple verb phrases. ► present simple ► past simple

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using basic present or past main verbs

positives: I love your cooking.
She lived in a small village.
negatives: I am walking right now.
He has been waiting for hours.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by a 'to'- infinitive.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + to infinitive for intentions and preferences

positives: I want to go to the park.
She hopes to see you soon.
negatives: I like the beautiful zoo.
I want an apple right now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would like to' + infinitive.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: would like to + infinitive

positives: I would like to visit the museum.
She'd really like to join us.
negatives: I like to visit the museum.
I would love to join us.

can_do_statement: Can use 'like' followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: like + to/ing

positives: I like to read books.
He likes swimming in the ocean.
negatives: I like the interesting books.
She likes the beautiful ocean.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there is' + singular noun phrase as complement.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'There is' introduces the existence of one thing.

positives: My home is nice, there is a nice garden.
In my home there's a kitchen.
negatives: There are two bedrooms in my house.
There was a big library.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there are' + plural noun phrase as complement.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'There are' introduces the existence of multiple things.

positives: There are two bathrooms in my apartment.
I think, in the park there are animals.
negatives: There is a nice garden outside.
There were many people at the party.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verb 'be' with complements.

ontology.mental_model: Linking an entity to a state or attribute using the copula.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'be' to describe something or someone.

positives: Because today is my birthday.
Martin is from Poland.
negatives: He is running fast.
They were playing outside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'but' to join a limited range of common adjectives, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: contrastive layering of attributes on one entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: paint then correct the picture

positives: The game was safe but boring.
It was cheap but nice.
negatives: He is tall but he is slow.
I was tired but I went to work.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of two syllables ending in '-y' by changing the 'y' to an 'I' and adding '-er'.

ontology.mental_model: y-roots shift spelling on the comparison scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: y becomes i on the ladder

positives: This is an easier question to answer.
She is a happier person now.
negatives: It is much easier.
He arrived earlier.

can_do_statement: Can use comparative adjectives attributively, before nouns.

ontology.mental_model: comparison glued to the noun it ranks
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the ranked noun

positives: I want a better car.
She needs a bigger house.
negatives: It is better than the iPad.
It's better that you say.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives from adjectives of one syllable by adding '-er'.

ontology.mental_model: one-syllable roots take the bare -er suffix
ontology.pedagogical_hook: short word, add er

positives: He is an older man.
I bought a cheaper car.
negatives: He runs much faster.
It is slightly smaller.

can_do_statement: Can form a range of comparative adjective phrases using 'more' + longer adjectives (usually three or more syllables).

ontology.pedagogical_hook: long word? let more do the work

negatives: I need more money.
She speaks more slowly.
positives: I think you must be more careful.
It was more expensive than the other clothes.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable ending in 'e', by adding '-r'.

ontology.mental_model: silent e stays, r attaches directly
ontology.pedagogical_hook: e already there, just add r

positives: We want a larger room.
It is a safer place.
negatives: I will see you later.
They walked closer.

can_do_statement: Can use comparative adjectives as a complement of 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: be hands the subject its position on the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: be + the scale point

positives: I think it would be easier.
The new one is better.
negatives: It is better than the iPad.
They are easier to understand.

can_do_statement: Can form irregular comparative adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: root swaps entirely on the scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the word jumps the ladder

negatives: She runs faster than me.
It is easier now.
positives: What colour do you think is better?
For further information, contact us.

can_do_statement: Can form comparative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable with a short vowel, by doubling the final consonant and adding '-er'

ontology.mental_model: short vowel locks the consonant before -er
ontology.pedagogical_hook: double it, then er

positives: I need a bigger room for this.
We are looking for a hotter climate.
negatives: Usually the bigger.
The weather is a lot hotter.

can_do_statement: Can use a comparative adjective with 'than' to compare two nouns or noun phrases.► comparative clauses

ontology.mental_model: than names the rival scale point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: name the rival

positives: My car is faster than yours.
This book is more interesting than that one.
negatives: I travel more than you do.
He has more free time than me.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' with common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: the scale tips past the usable point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: over the limit

positives: This box is too heavy.
The soup is too hot.
negatives: I ate too much yesterday.
There are too many cars here.

can_do_statement: Can form adjective phrases with a very limited range of adjectives + a prepositional phrase.

ontology.mental_model: the attribute points at a location or target
ontology.pedagogical_hook: point the adjective

positives: It is different from the normal cement.
It would be good for the environment.
negatives: I would like to speak good with him.
I think it's good because keep practicing.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' + adjective + prepositional phrase

ontology.mental_model: excess measured against a person or thing
ontology.pedagogical_hook: too much, for whom?

positives: The shirt is too small for me.
It is too hot in the summer.
negatives: It is too small to read.
There are too many in the room.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs of degree ('really', 'so', 'quite') with an increasing range of common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: really, so, quite set different volume levels
ontology.pedagogical_hook: pick the volume

positives: It is really difficult.
The weather is so nice.
negatives: It was a really difficult situation.
It is a really big city.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives ('main', 'only') that limit the noun that they go before.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: limiting adjectives

positives: This is the main reason I came here.
He was the only person who understood.
negatives: I only want to sleep for a bit.
The water main broke yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adjectives predicatively, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: be hands the attribute to the subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: say it after be

detection.regex_triage: \b(?:i am|you are|he is|she is|it is|we are|they are|i was|you were|he was|she was|it was|we were|they were)\s+(free|friendly|happy|tired|ready|busy|kind|lovely|beautiful|nice)\b

positives: I was tired.
They are friendly.
negatives: You are a rich person.
It is difficult.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adjectives predicatively, after linking verbs 'look' and 'feel'.

ontology.mental_model: look and feel pipe the attribute through the senses
ontology.pedagogical_hook: sense it, then say it

positives: I feel comfortable in Paris.
She looks happy today.
negatives: I feel bad about it.
He looks angry.

can_do_statement: Can form a limited range of complex noun phrases with a superlative adjective  + prepositional phrase, to talk about something unique.► noun phrases ►  clauses: comparison

ontology.mental_model: a superlative plus a set-specifier phrase carves out the single unique member
ontology.pedagogical_hook: name the thing, then name the world it beats
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions an entity as one-of-everything

positives: She is the best player in the team.
It is the biggest company of corn.
negatives: He is the best of the players.
It is the best.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of prepositional phrases with 'of' after a superlative adjective, to refer to one thing within a set or part of a set.

ontology.mental_model: 'of' names the set from which the ranked member is drawn
ontology.pedagogical_hook: best of WHAT? - of names the pile
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker picks one thing out of a stated set

positives: He is the best of us.
That was the hardest of the tests.
negatives: It is one of the best tests.
She is the best.

can_do_statement: Can use prepositional phrases with 'in' + singular name of a place after a superlative adjective.

ontology.mental_model: 'in' names the spatial container that bounds the comparison set
ontology.pedagogical_hook: biggest WHERE? - in names the place
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the top-ranked thing inside a place

positives: It is the biggest in the world.
He is the best player in the team.
negatives: It is the best in places.
The political influence in the decision is huge.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the '-est' suffix, with adjectives of one syllable, and with two-syllable adjectives ending in -y.

ontology.mental_model: the -est / -iest suffix stamps a word as rank-one on a scale
ontology.pedagogical_hook: y becomes i before you crown it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades things to the top rung

positives: He is the smartest boy in the class.
This is the easiest way to learn.
negatives: I will do my honest work.
They went into the dark forest.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'my' or 'your' + superlative adjective + noun, with a limited range of nouns and contexts. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: a possessive determiner hands the top rank to a person
ontology.pedagogical_hook: my + the-most-thing + noun
ontology.agency_or_distance: possessive ties the superlative to an involved party

positives: He is my best friend.
That was your biggest mistake.
negatives: She is my honest friend.
It was his best performance.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives with adjectives of one syllable with a short vowel, by doubling the final consonant and adding '–est'.

ontology.mental_model: short-vowel words double their last consonant before taking the crown
ontology.pedagogical_hook: big -> bigger -> the BIGGEST - hold the consonant
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks top rank with doubled-consonant spelling

positives: It is the biggest.
This is the hottest.
negatives: It is the most biggest city.
This is the most hottest.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'the' + superlative adjective + noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: 'the' plus a -est adjective flags exactly one noun as peak of its kind
ontology.pedagogical_hook: the + -est + thing
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker presents the ranking as given, unique

positives: It is the tallest building in town.
She is the best player on the team.
negatives: He is the honest man.
It is the main goal.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives using the suffix '-st' to adjectives ending in '–e'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: superlative adjectives ending in e

positives: This is the largest building in the city.
She is the nicest person I have ever met.
negatives: This is the biggest building in town.
He is my greatest friend.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjectives by adding the suffix '-est', to adjectives of one syllable.

ontology.mental_model: a one-syllable adjective bolts -est on the end to claim top rank
ontology.pedagogical_hook: old, older, the OLD - est
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker asserts an absolute peak on a scale

positives: It is the biggest company here.
He was my fastest runner.
negatives: It is the most biggest city.
It is one of the 3 biggest cities.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the' with a limited range of superlative adjectives without a following noun, when the noun is understood.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying the extreme point on a scale without explicitly naming the entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When you already know what we're talking about, just say 'the best' instead of 'the best thing'.
ontology.agency_or_distance: High conceptual distance (referencing an abstract peak).

positives: My relatives gave me presents but the computer game was the best.
But Mark's present was the most beautiful!
negatives: It is the best book I have ever read.
That is the most beautiful car.

can_do_statement: Can form superlative adjective phrases using 'the most', with longer adjectives of two or more syllables.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the most + adjective — stamp a multi-syllable adjective as rank-one
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker grades two-plus-syllable adjectives to the top

positives: It was the most beautiful day of my life.
This is the most expensive car here.
negatives: He took the most of the food.
That is the most biggest problem.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('so much', 'a lot') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity. ► determiners

ontology.pedagogical_hook: so much / a lot — amplify the verb to maximum volume
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker cranks the speaker-level of feeling or action

positives: I am looking forward to seeing you so much!
We listened to music and we danced a lot too.
negatives: He is so kind to me.
I love you more than anything.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('also', 'so', 'however') to show a relationship between two clauses or sentences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: also / so / however — wire two ideas into one discourse
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker binds clauses into a relationship of addition, result, or contrast

positives: I was tired, so I went to bed.
He likes cats, however John is allergic.
negatives: He is so strong.
So I went to the store.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('yesterday', 'just', 'now', 'already',) to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: yesterday / just / now / already — pin the event to a point on the speech-time line
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker anchors the event relative to S

positives: Yesterday I went shopping.
I've just seen your mail.
negatives: I went home and rested.
She came over later.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of manner adverbs and adverb phrases to modify how something happens.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: manner adverbs

positives: He played the guitar very well.
She ran fast to catch the bus.
negatives: It was a very fast car.
The wood on the table is very hard.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('usually', 'often', 'never', 'weekly') to talk about frequency.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: frequency adverbs

positives: I usually wake up at seven o'clock.
She often visits her grandmother on Sundays.
negatives: I bought a weekly magazine at the store.
The monthly payment is due tomorrow.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs ('so', 'quite', 'too') to modify adjectives.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: degree adverbs with adjectives

positives: The movie was so boring.
This car is too expensive for me.
negatives: I want to go there too.
He ran quite quickly.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('only', 'just') to focus on or point to something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: only / just — spotlight a single element, dimming the rest
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent from a presumed larger set

positives: It's only two hours.
I have only one chance.
negatives: I went home and rested.
She plays football.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('first', 'then', 'after that') to order segments of discourse.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: first / then / after that — map the events onto a timeline
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker arranges discourse events in chronological order

positives: First, I went to the mall.
And then, she started crying.
negatives: I was the first person there.
First thing I do is sleep.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('actually', 'unfortunately', 'of course', 'I’m sorry') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: simply / truly / surely / apparently / naturally / surprisingly / inevitably — finer-grained stance markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks nuanced distance from the proposition

positives: Obviously everybody has the right to be on a strike.
We can't truly blame ourselves.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.
She finished her homework.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('maybe', 'perhaps') to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — finer-grained certainty markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: And it will probably be on TV next month!
If I were you I'd certainly choose not to go.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.
She finished her homework.

guideword: FORM: TIME  and SEQUENCING, MODIFYING CLAUSES
can_do_statement: Can use time and sequencing adverbs to modify clauses and sentences.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an entire event with a time or sequence marker
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start your sentence with words like 'Yesterday' or 'First' to set the scene.

positives: Yesterday I went shopping and bought some clothes.
First we had dinner in my house and after we went to the pub.
negatives: The first time I saw her was magical.
I need a today newspaper.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of manner adverbs to modify verbs.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use common words like 'fast' or 'well' to describe how you do something.

positives: They swam very fast.
I learned to use my phone very quickly.
negatives: It is a very fast car.
The well is very deep.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of degree adverbs to modify common gradable adjectives.

ontology.mental_model: Scaling the intensity of a property
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'so', 'really', or 'too' before adjectives to change their strength.

positives: I'm so happy because you can come!
But it is too expensive.
negatives: I really like it.
He runs so fast.

can_do_statement: Can use manner adverbs in the usual end position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + well/quickly/slowly/loudly — slot the manner adverb at the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker describes how the action was performed at the end

positives: Please answer me quickly because there are only eleven tickets.
She drives carefully on icy roads.
negatives: I went to the bank.
She finished her homework.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs in mid position between the subject and the main verb and after modal verbs, auxiliary verbs and 'be'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: subject + can/will/be + adverb + main verb — slot the adverb after aux/modal/be
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker places the adverb in the medial slot

positives: I have always loved reading novels.
She is probably going to arrive late.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She left her book here.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs before an adjective.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: so / quite / too + adjective — turn the adjective to a non-default intensity

positives: I'm so glad you are coming.
They are quite expensive.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She left her book here.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs in front position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: However / Furthermore / Moreover / Actually — slot a wider set of adverbials at the clause head
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker opens the clause with a wider set of framing adverbials

positives: However I can study only on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.
Furthermore, the cost is much lower this year.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She finished her homework.

can_do_statement: Can use degree adverbs in end position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + a lot / so much / very much — push the degree to the clause tail
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker amplifies degree at the end of the clause

positives: I like it a lot.
He helped me so much!
negatives: I have a lot of time.
She has so much money.

can_do_statement: Can use evaluative, viewpoint and sequencing adverbs outside the clause, in front position, as a cohesive device to link to a previous statement in a preceding clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Actually / However / Fortunately / Interestingly / In addition — fronted adverbs as cohesion hooks
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker head-loads a discourse link into the next clause

positives: Actually I want you to decide what colour my room should be.
Fortunately, the train was on time that morning.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She finished her homework.

can_do_statement: Can modify a limited range of adverbs of time, degree, and manner with other adverbs.

ontology.mental_model: Refining the temporal or manner frame of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combining basic adverbs for precise time or degree

positives: I love it so much.
I really need it right now.
negatives: It is so big.
I am right here.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be' + 'like' + noun or pronoun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing identity or form

positives: I like her because she is like me.
It's like a little train.
negatives: I really like pizza.
Would you like a drink?

can_do_statement: Can combine multiple main clauses, with commas and conjunctions expressing order, often to give instructions or directions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Giving directions using 'and' or 'then'

positives: Go straight ahead, then turn right, and walk to the end.
Turn down the street, and then go straight, so you'll see it.
negatives: I like apples and oranges.
He went home because he was tired.

can_do_statement: Can form an affirmative imperative with the base form of a main verb.

positives: Bring your swim-suit for the swimming pool.
Call me if you need anything.
negatives: You bring your swim-suit every day.
Calling me was a big mistake.

guideword: FORM: NEGATIVE DECLARATIVE, MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
can_do_statement: Can form a simple negative declarative clause with modal verb + 'not' or 'n't'.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing inability, prohibition, or negative future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating modal verbs

positives: You won't have to bring anything.
I couldn't come to my party.
negatives: I will come.
Can't you see?

can_do_statement: Can form a simple negative declarative clause with auxiliary 'have' + 'not' or 'n't' and 'have' + 'not' or 'n't (got)'

ontology.mental_model: Expressing lack of completion or lack of possession
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating perfect aspect or possession

positives: I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time.
I hadn't got any clothes for summer.
negatives: I have not.
Have you seen it?

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to give instructions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Route Script — issuing sequenced commands that walk the listener through a procedure or a journey.

positives: Turn left at the corner.
Go straight past the bank.
negatives: Go wrong and then right.
Go to the prison.

can_do_statement: Can use negative imperative after an instruction, for emphasis.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Second Nail — driving the warning home after the instruction has already landed.

positives: Call me, don't forget.
Keep trying, don't give up.
negatives: No, don't worry.
Don't give up, don't give up.

can_do_statement: Can use 'let's' + base form of a main verb, for first person plural imperatives to make a suggestion.

positives: Yes, let's get a pizza tonight.
Let's play outside.
negatives: Let's see what happens.
Let's talk about it.

can_do_statement: Can form a negative imperative with the auxiliary verb 'do' + 'n't' + base form of a main verb, to give advice, instructions or orders.

positives: Don't touch that button.
Don't go there alone.
negatives: Don't worry about it.
Don't mind me.

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to give instructions, often at the end of a letter or when saying goodbye to someone.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Channel Keep-Alive — closing the letter with an action-token that holds the connection open.

positives: Write to me soon.
Call me back.
negatives: Take care of the garden for me.
I will call you back later.

guideword: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE INTERROGATIVE, WITH MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS
can_do_statement: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) with modal auxiliary verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Asking for permission, predicting, or requesting
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Yes/no questions with modals

positives: Would you like to come with me?
Can I come tomorrow to collect it?
negatives: I can come tomorrow.
What will you do?

can_do_statement: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) with auxiliary 'be' and 'have'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Yes/no questions with be or have

positives: Are you going to the new art class?
Have you got a new dress for the party?
negatives: You are going to the art class.
Where have you been?

can_do_statement: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) of main lexical verbs with auxiliary 'do'.

ontology.mental_model: Querying about habits or past events
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Yes/no questions with do

positives: Do you remember Julie?
Did you buy a new mobile phone?
negatives: I do remember Julie.
What did you buy?

can_do_statement: Can form 'wh-' interrogative clauses with a 'wh-' word as object.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Wh- questions

positives: When are you coming here?
What have you bought?
negatives: Do you know when he arrived?
Who came to the party?

can_do_statement: Can use 'What a pity' + ('that') clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing regret or disappointment over a situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'what a pity' followed by a clause to express feelings.

positives: What a pity that you couldn't make it.
What a pity it rained all day.
negatives: It's a pity.
She felt pity for the poor dog.

can_do_statement: Can use 'What a' + noun phrase and 'What a' + noun phrase + clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing strong emotion or surprise about a noun.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'what a' for exclamations.

positives: What a brilliant idea!
What a nice surprise.
negatives: I don't know what a dog is.
What a pity you couldn't stay.

can_do_statement: Can form negative interrogative clauses.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using negative forms in questions.

positives: Isn't it a wonderful day?
Don't you want to come?
negatives: He isn't here right now.
Wouldn't it be wonderful!

can_do_statement: Can form negative 'wh-' interrogative clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Suggesting actions or asking for reasons.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using WH-words with negative auxiliaries.

positives: Why don't we go to the park?
What couldn't you understand?
negatives: I don't know why he isn't here.
Tell me what didn't work.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'who' as the subject.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying a specific person within a group.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' as the subject in a defining relative clause.

positives: I need a friend who really listens to me.
The man who is standing there is my brother.
negatives: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
I don't know who did it.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' as the subject in a defining relative clause.

positives: I want a car which runs fast.
He read a book which changed his life.
negatives: The house, which is red, is nice.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'that' as the object.

ontology.mental_model: Providing more info about a noun by acting as the object of a relative clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'that' as the object in a defining relative clause.

positives: The team that I like won.
I bought clothes that I need.
negatives: I know that he is here.
That is my car.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'who' as the subject.

ontology.mental_model: Adding extra, non-essential information about a person.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' in a non-defining relative clause.

positives: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
I saw Mary, who was walking her dog.
negatives: The man who is standing there is my brother.
I don't know who did it.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject,.

ontology.mental_model: Adding extra, non-essential information about a thing.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' in a non-defining relative clause.

positives: My car, which is red, is very fast.
I read that book, which was very interesting.
negatives: The car which I bought is red.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'which' as the object.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying a specific thing as the object.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' as the object in a defining relative clause.

positives: The computer game which I borrowed is great.
The colour which I prefer is pink.
negatives: The game, which I borrowed, is great.
I don't know which game you mean.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'which' as the object.

ontology.mental_model: Linking secondary descriptive information to a main noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a non-defining relative clause with 'which' to add extra, non-essential information
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance from core clause by adding optional descriptive layer

positives: The best of all was a marble statue, which my aunt gave me.
I liked the book, which I received a few days ago.
negatives: The best of all was a marble statue, which sat on the table.
This is the car which I bought.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause, without a relative pronoun.

ontology.mental_model: Defining a noun implicitly by attaching a subject and verb directly
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Dropping the relative pronoun in defining clauses when it is the object
ontology.agency_or_distance: Efficiency in communication by omitting redundant syntactic markers

positives: The clothes I wore were old.
Here is the information you want.
negatives: I know that you want it.
She said that I am wrong.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-finite subordinate clause with 'to', to introduce purpose.

ontology.mental_model: Stating the purpose or goal of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Infinitive of purpose

positives: To reach my house, you just have to turn left.
I went to the store to buy some milk.
negatives: I want to go to the park.
She gave the book to him.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with time conjunctions, before or after a main clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Time clauses with when/while

positives: I feel comfortable when I am wearing these clothes.
While we were eating pizza, the phone rang.
negatives: I don't know when he will arrive.
The meeting is after lunch.

can_do_statement: Can use an 'if-' clause ('if you want', 'like', 'prefer') to soften the directness of imperatives, offers or suggestions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Hedging with 'if you want/like/prefer'.

positives: Bring some films if you want.
Please, come here wearing a white T-shirt and a skirt, or shorts if you prefer.
negatives: If you go to the store, buy milk.
If you are tired, go to sleep.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE, REAL CONDITIONS
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple with present simple, 'can' or imperative in the main clause to refer to things that are true now or very likely to happen.

ontology.mental_model: Establishing a general truth or likely condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Zero or first conditional for real conditions.

positives: If I have spare time I always read a book.
You can get to my house if you take the number 35 bus.
negatives: If you had time, you could go.
There are no ifs or buts about it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple, with an imperative in the main clause.

ontology.mental_model: Giving an instruction based on a condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: If clause with imperative main clause.

positives: If you find it, call me.
If you want to come, just tell me.
negatives: If you find it, you will be happy.
If you want to come, you can.

can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clause with 'if' + present simple.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: General 'if + present simple' structure.

positives: If you buy a gift for me, please buy a book, because I love to read.
If you agree, we can go shopping after the film.
negatives: If you wanted, we could go.
If you bought it, I would pay.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of simple subordinating conjunctions '(if, when, so, while)' to introduce a subordinate clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: basic subordinators

positives: If I need a camera, I will use my mobile phone.
My father said that I should use green, but I don't like green, so I decided to use blue.
negatives: I am so happy.
I'll do it if and when.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the' + adjectives in a noun phrase, to specify.

ontology.mental_model: Specificity marked by definite article plus attribute.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the' with descriptive adjectives to point to a very specific object.

positives: My house is opposite the new cafe.
I think it's on the red sofa.
negatives: It is a new cafe.
I bought a red sofa.

can_do_statement: Can form a noun phrase with 'the' + superlative adjectives + noun.

ontology.mental_model: Definite article paired with extreme degree attributes.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Superlatives single out the absolute pinnacle, requiring 'the'.

positives: It has the latest technology.
La Baule is the biggest beach.
negatives: It is a big beach.
He wants a fast car.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with uncountable nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular, or uncountable entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or substance.

positives: I need this information right now.
This luggage is very heavy.
negatives: This topic is interesting.
This block is very hard.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' with singular nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'that' specific item.

positives: I read that book yesterday.
That tutor was very helpful to me.
negatives: Things that helped me a lot.
I think that makes perfect sense.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' to talk about or point to things which are further away in time and space from the speaker or writer

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'that' specific item or place.

positives: Look at that building over there.
I remember that day clearly.
negatives: Look at this building.
I remember this day.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' to refer to something with immediate relevance which has already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities with immediate relevance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'this' specific thing just discussed.

positives: I bought a new dress, and this dress is amazing.
We have a serious problem. How do we solve this problem?
negatives: A dress is not this expensive.
The problem with this is clear.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in an increasing range of contexts to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ► pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or place.

positives: I am writing this letter to you.
You can contact me on this number.
negatives: I am writing a letter.
You can contact me on that number.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' in an increasing range of contexts to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view. ► noun phrases ► pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, singular entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'this' specific item or place.

positives: I am writing this letter to tell you about my present.
You can contact me by calling me this number.
negatives: I am writing a letter.
You can contact me on that number.

can_do_statement: Can use 'these' with plural nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, plural entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'these' specific items.

positives: These conversations are always helpful.
I love these beautiful flowers.
negatives: These are my favorite books.
All these for Mexico.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' to refer to something which has already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'that' specific thing previously mentioned.

positives: You should go that shop.
I want to study that course.
negatives: You should go this shop.
I want to study this course.

can_do_statement: Can use 'these' to refer to places and things from the speaker's or writer's point of view.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of specific, plural entities in the immediate context.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Pointing to 'these' specific items or places.

positives: Look at these old shoes.
These beautiful places are nice.
negatives: I hate these new rules.
These topics are hard.

can_do_statement: Can use 'those' to refer to things which have already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Referencing previously mentioned entities at a distance.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring back to 'those' specific things previously mentioned.

positives: I bought those clothes because I'm going to Japan.
It is black and pink, I like those colours very much.
negatives: I bought these clothes.
I like these colours.

can_do_statement: Can use 'these' to refer to things with immediate relevance or which have already been mentioned. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: Proximal demonstrative pointing to previously mentioned multiple entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'These' links back to specific plural items just discussed.

positives: These places are very old.
I will need these things because it is summer.
negatives: I don't like this place.
Those things are useless.

can_do_statement: Can use 'those' to talk about or point to things which the speaker or writer perceives to be further away in time and space.

ontology.mental_model: Distal demonstrative pointing to entities further away.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Those' is used for plural nouns that are distant in space or time.

positives: Look at those birds in the sky.
Those mountains are beautiful from here.
negatives: These birds are very loud.
That mountain is tall.

can_do_statement: Can use 'those' with plural nouns. ► noun phrases ►  pronouns: demonstrative

ontology.mental_model: General distal demonstrative for plural entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Those' refers to plural items, distinguishing them from 'these'.

positives: The cost of those clothes was high.
I love to play those instruments.
negatives: I want these clothes.
That instrument is loud.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' after singular or proper nouns to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: I found my sister's jacket.
We are going to Linda's party.
negatives: It's raining outside today.
He's running very fast.

can_do_statement: Can use quantifying determiners + possessive determiners + 'of' + noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: All of my friends were there.
Bring some of your DVDs.
negatives: Some friends were there.
I saw all the cars.

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in negative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying uncountable entities in absence or low quantity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not much' to describe a small amount of something you can't count.

positives: We didn't have much money for the trip.
I haven't got much time to watch television.
negatives: We had much money for the trip.
She hasn't seen many friends lately.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('each', 'an', 'one' and numbers).

ontology.mental_model: Specifying exact quantities or individual components of a group.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'each', 'an', 'one', or numbers to talk about single items.

positives: Each class is about one hour long.
We have an extra ticket for the concert.
negatives: All classes are long.
We have some extra tickets.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners ('some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of') with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns.
