ontology.mental_model: Expressing indefinite quantities for both countable and uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of' for things you have many of, or can't count.

positives: I think we should bring some water.
There were no clouds in the sky.
negatives: I think we should bring a bottle.
There was not a cloud.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('all', 'both', 'a few').

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying plural entities as totalities or small subsets.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all', 'both', or 'a few' to talk about multiple things.

positives: This notice is for all students.
I'm just writing to tell you a few things.
negatives: This notice is for every student.
I'm just writing to tell you one thing.

can_do_statement: Can use 'many' with plural nouns in negative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing absence of a large quantity for countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not many' to say there are only a few of something.

positives: There aren't many tickets left.
I haven't got many winter clothes.
negatives: There are many tickets.
I haven't got much time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so many' and 'too many' with plural nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so many' or 'too many' to exaggerate a lot of things.

positives: We played so many games together.
I know I bought too many things.
negatives: We played many games.
I know I bought too much food.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', number + 'of', 'each of'). ► pronouns: quantity

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', or numbers with 'of the' or 'of my'.

positives: I spent all of my money!
Some of my friends gave me books.
negatives: I spent all my money!
Some friends gave me books.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'AS YOU KNOW', ORGANISING, MARKING SHARED KNOWLEDGE
can_do_statement: Can use 'as you know' as a discourse marker of shared knowledge.

ontology.mental_model: Signalling that the following information is already part of the listener's knowledge.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'as you know' to build rapport.

positives: As you know, I live in England.
Because, as you know, I am leaving tomorrow.
negatives: I know you as a good person.
As you can see, it is raining.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so' as a discourse marker to summarise, usually in informal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Summarising or deducing consequences in conversational contexts.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so' at the start of a clause to summarise.

positives: So, what do you think?
So I'll be at your house at 15.30.
negatives: I am so tired.
He ran so quickly.

can_do_statement: Can use prepositional phrases in the front position for focus.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Setting the scene before the main event

positives: In the morning, we usually go for a walk.
From my window, I can see the whole city.
negatives: We usually go for a walk in the morning.
I can see the whole city from my window.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: Visualizing an action in progress at a point in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'will be -ing' to describe an ongoing action in the future.

positives: I'll be waiting for you at the station.
We will be starting at noon.
negatives: I will be there on time.
She is waiting for you now.

can_do_statement: Can use the future continuous with 'will' to talk about an event or action in progress at a specified time in the future.

ontology.mental_model: Connecting a future time expression with an ongoing action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combine 'Tomorrow' or 'Tonight' with 'will be -ing' for future plans.

positives: Tomorrow I'll be working in the morning.
Tonight we will be resting.
negatives: I'll be working later today.
Tomorrow I will work hard.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms 'will not' and 'won't'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'won't' and 'will not' for negative future.

positives: Without them I will not be able to play football.
I won't be at home before seven.
negatives: I will be at home.
I want to go home.

can_do_statement: Can use the question forms of 'will' and 'shall'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming questions about the future using 'will' or 'shall' subject inversion.

positives: Will you come?
What shall I bring?
negatives: I will definitely come.
We shall go together.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form 'shall' with 'I' and 'we'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'shall' with first-person subjects for affirmative statements.

positives: I shall come with you.
We shall take a bus to the sports centre.
negatives: Shall we go together?
He shall arrive soon.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall I' to make offers.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'shall I' to kindly offer assistance.

positives: Shall I wait for you?
Shall I buy you one?
negatives: I shall wait for you.
Shall we wait for them?

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to make requests.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will you' to request action from someone else.

positives: Will you come tomorrow to my house?
Will you send it for me?
negatives: You will come tomorrow.
Will they come tomorrow?

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to ask about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' in question form to inquire about what someone intends to do.

positives: Will you have a mobile phone?
Will they come by train?
negatives: I will have a mobile phone.
They will come by train.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall we' to make suggestions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'shall we' to suggest a shared activity.

positives: Shall we go to my friend's house to get it?
Shall we go there together?
negatives: We shall go there together.
Shall I go there?

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to express willingness.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: My mother will drive us there.
I will certainly help you with your homework.
negatives: I have a strong will.
She filed her will with the lawyer.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative and question forms of 'be going to' talk about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I'm going to use pink paint.
My mum is going to take us by car.
negatives: I am going to the store.
He is going to school right now.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: What are you going to wear?
Are you going to come tomorrow evening?
negatives: Are you going to the party?
Why are they going to the mall?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I'm going to wear them on holiday.
It is going to start at half past four.
negatives: Are we going to study?
I am going to the library.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be going to' with 'be' to make predictions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: This Saturday is going to be a nice day.
It's going to be fantastic.
negatives: I am going to see him.
We are going to play football.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about future arrangements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: present continuous for arrangements (A2)

positives: I am working this Saturday morning.
We're having the meal at 7pm.
negatives: I work every Saturday.
I was working all day yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to ask about future plans.

ontology.mental_model: inquiry about fixed arrangement in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: present continuous for future questions (A2)

positives: Are you coming to the party tonight?
When is John going to the store?
negatives: Do you work on weekends?
I am coming to the party.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with 'when' to refer to the future.

ontology.mental_model: future event dependent on another event
ontology.pedagogical_hook: present simple with 'when' for future

positives: I'll tell you more when I meet you.
Can you call me when you find it?
negatives: When did you arrive?
I saw him when I left.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple to talk about timetabled events in the future.

ontology.mental_model: fixed future event based on a timetable
ontology.pedagogical_hook: present simple for timetables

positives: It begins on 8 o'clock in the evening.
The train leaves at 6 pm.
negatives: The class started at 6 pm.
It is finishing at 7 pm.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with 'I hope' to talk about hopes and wishes for the future.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: present simple with 'hope'

positives: I hope you enjoy your holiday too.
We hope that he arrives safely.
negatives: I hoped you would come.
I hope to see you soon.

can_do_statement: Can use 'I' + 'be' + 'sure' + clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Expressing confidence in a statement

positives: I'm sure I can beat you at chess.
I am not sure what I want to do.
negatives: Are you sure about this?
He is sure that we will win.

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' to give and refuse permission or talk about what is forbidden.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker establishes rules or boundaries about allowed actions for a second party.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'you can' or 'you can't' to tell someone what they are allowed or not allowed to do.

positives: You can wear anything you want.
You cannot bring your mobile phone.
negatives: Can you come on Sunday?
I can play the piano.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' + 'be able to' + infinitive to talk about possibility and ability.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Predicting ability

positives: I won't be able to finish this tonight.
Will you be able to help me tomorrow?
negatives: I am able to swim very well.
She will be there soon.

can_do_statement: Can use the question forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: have (got) to question

positives: What do you have to wear?
Have you got to bring a pencil?
negatives: I have to go now.
She has got to win.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: have (got) to negative

positives: You don't have to bring many things with you.
We haven't got to bring anything with us.
negatives: I have to go.
She hasn't a clue.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: have (got) to affirmative

positives: This weekend I have to go to a party.
You have got to bring a cap.
negatives: I have a dog.
He got to the station.

can_do_statement: Can use 'have (got) to' to talk about obligations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: have (got) to obligation

positives: We have to go before then.
You have to bring your swimming costume.
negatives: They have a nice house.
She got to work early.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: may + verb

positives: I may need some help later.
It may be dirty.
negatives: I may not be able to come.
May I help you?

can_do_statement: Can use 'may' to talk about weak possibility referring to the present and the future.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: may for possibility

positives: It may rain later.
We may need your help tomorrow.
negatives: May I ask a question?
I may not want to go.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To talk about something that is possible, use 'might' with a base verb.

positives: The weather might be hot and sunny.
I think it might be in your bedroom.
negatives: It might not be true.
I shouldn't do this.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might' to talk about weak possibility.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: If something is only a small possibility, use 'might' instead of 'will'.

positives: He might take us.
It might be on the computer table.
negatives: I might not know.
I shouldn't do this.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Prohibition

positives: You mustn't forget to call.
They must not leave the area.
negatives: You must go there.
I must find it.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Obligation

positives: You must wear a helmet.
I must go now.
negatives: You mustn't do that.
They must not touch it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' with a limited range of pronouns ('I' and 'you') to talk about obligation and necessity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Personal obligation

positives: I must finish this today.
You must take your keys.
negatives: He must finish it.
They must take their keys.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall I' to make offers.

ontology.mental_model: Volunteering action by questioning one's own future action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Shall I' to offer help or ask what someone wants you to do.

positives: Shall I carry those bags?
Shall I open the window?
negatives: I shall do it.
We shall overcome.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Shall' acts like 'will', usually with I or We.

positives: We shall arrive at noon.
I shall see you then.
negatives: Shall we go?
They shall not pass.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall' with 'we' to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Proposing a joint future action to a listener.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Shall we' to make a suggestion to do something together.

positives: Shall we dance?
Shall we eat now?
negatives: We shall overcome.
I shall weigh my options.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form.

ontology.mental_model: Seeking direction, advice, or making a proposal via a question.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Shall' inverted with subject for questions.

positives: What shall I do?
Shall we begin?
negatives: We shall meet tomorrow.
I shall not go.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.mental_model: Advising against an action or state.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Should not' or 'shouldn't'.

positives: You shouldn't miss it.
You should not wear that.
negatives: You should miss it.
They should go.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'should' in affirmative sentences.

positives: You should come at six.
We should go there together.
negatives: You shouldn't go.
He should have gone.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Should' before the subject to form a question.

positives: Should I wear special clothes?
Where should we go?
negatives: You should go.
They shouldn't come.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should' to give advice.

ontology.mental_model: Directing someone else's action for their benefit.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'you should' to give someone advice.

positives: You should buy this.
You should take some money.
negatives: I should go now.
He should try harder.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should' to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Proposing a good idea for someone else to follow.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Give advice to a friend using 'you should'.

positives: I think we should meet at 2 pm.
You should bring your guitar.
negatives: It should be a good day.
You should have been there.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to ask about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Questions about the future

positives: Will you come by bus?
When will they arrive?
negatives: I will come by bus.
She will arrive tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Future questions

positives: Will you be at home?
What time will you be here?
negatives: I will be at home.
He won't be here.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Future negative statements

positives: You won't need anything.
I hope it will not be boring.
negatives: I will come.
Will you be there?

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to talk about willingness and offers

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Offering help

positives: My mother will get us there.
I'll help you with that.
negatives: I will be 20 next week.
It will rain tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' in the main clause after an 'if-' clause to talk about possible future situations. ► conditionals

ontology.pedagogical_hook: First conditional

positives: If I need a camera, I will use my mobile phone.
If you can help me, I will be very happy.
negatives: I will use my mobile phone.
If I need a camera, I use my phone.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would not' for negative hypotheticals

positives: You wouldn't believe how much it costs.
I think we would not need that.
negatives: I would like to go there.
He couldn't do it at all.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would love/prefer' for strong choices

positives: I'd love to have a pen-friend.
I would prefer Sunday afternoon.
negatives: I would like a pen-friend.
I would not love that.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' with a wide range of verbs to talk about wishes and preferences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would love to' or 'would prefer to' with a verb

positives: I would prefer to go on Sunday.
I'd love to hear it!
negatives: I would prefer Sunday.
I'd love some hot tea.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it would be' to make suggestions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'it would be' to gently suggest

positives: It would be very good if you came with me.
It'd be nice to bring a game.
negatives: I would be happy to go.
It will be nice to see you.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to talk about imagined situations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would' with base verbs for hypothetical scenarios

positives: It would look awesome in my room.
It would be fun there.
negatives: I would like some tea.
I would have done it already.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form 'would you like'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would you like' to offer or invite.

positives: Would you like to play tennis?
I'm going to a concert, would you like to come?
negatives: Do you like tennis?
I would like some water.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs of certainty and possibility ('maybe', 'perhaps'), before a clause or ellipted clause. ► adverbs: position

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Introducing possibilities at the start of a phrase

positives: Maybe we could visit that park.
Perhaps it's in the kitchen under the table.
negatives: I don't know, maybe.
That is perhaps true.

guideword: FORM/USE: MID POSITION, HEDGING OR EMPHASIS
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs in mid position or after main verb 'be', to modify an assertion, either through hedging or emphasis. ► adverbs: position

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Modifying certainty mid-sentence

positives: It is probably in the sitting room.
You should probably wear a T-shirt.
negatives: Probably, he will come.
I think so, definitely.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' to make requests.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'could you / we' for polite requests

positives: Could you help me to paint my bedroom?
Could we meet on Friday afternoon?
negatives: I could run fast when I was young.
Could he have done it?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form of 'could' to talk about inability.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'couldn't' for past inability

positives: I couldn't work without it.
She couldn't buy the T-shirt.
negatives: I could definitely do that.
Could you help me?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using affirmative 'could'

positives: You could come by bus.
We could go to the museum.
negatives: I couldn't close it.
Could you help me?

can_do_statement: Can use the question form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Inverting 'could' for questions

positives: Could you help me?
Could we meet on Friday?
negatives: I could close the window.
They couldn't see.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'could not' / 'couldn't'

positives: Too bad you couldn't come.
I could not close the window.
negatives: Could you bring it?
We could go there.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' with a limited range of verbs to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' + limited verbs (e.g., go, have, take) as a gentle directive or suggestion.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Suggesting ideas softly
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: offering a choice to the listener

positives: We could have dinner after that, if you want.
You could go to Versailles.
negatives: She could speak French when she was younger.
Could you pass the salt?

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of determiners as pronouns and indefinite pronouns in negative contexts.  ► Pronouns: quantity

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'any' or 'many' without a noun to refer back to something absent.

positives: I bought a shirt, because I haven't got any.
As regards close friends, I don't have many.
negatives: I don't have any money left.
She didn't see many friends.

can_do_statement: Can use negative forms of modal verbs. ► modal verbs

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating modal verbs like can, will, and should.

positives: I'm sorry I can't come to your wedding.
Sorry but I won't be in town on Wednesday 17th.
negatives: I will not only go there, but also help out.
Can you tell me what happened?

can_do_statement: Can form negative imperatives of main verbs with 'don’t' + main verb. ► Clauses: imperatives

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'Don't' at the start of a clause to give a negative command.

positives: Don't forget your electric guitar.
Please do not be late for the meeting.
negatives: I don't forget my friends.
They do not want to be late.

can_do_statement: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the present continuous and present perfect with 'be' and 'have' + 'not/n't'.  ► present continuous ► present perfect

ontology.mental_model: Current absence of action or experience
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating present continuous and present perfect with 'not'.

positives: The window is broken and is not closing.
Now, I haven't got any money.
negatives: I am not happy about it.
He has not the time to do this.

can_do_statement: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the past simple with 'didn’t' + main verb. ► past simple

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating past actions with 'didn't'.

positives: It was very sad that you didn't come to my birthday party.
I did not spend a lot of money.
negatives: I do not spend a lot of money.
He hasn't spent much money.

can_do_statement: Can use determiners 'any', 'much' and 'many' with nouns in negative contexts. ► Determiners: quantity

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'any', 'much', or 'many' with a noun in a negative sentence.

positives: I bought them because I didn't have any shirts.
I have only spent £25 because I haven't much money.
negatives: I didn't have any.
She didn't see much.

can_do_statement: Can use determiner 'no' with nouns.  ► Determiners: quantity

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'no' directly before a noun to signify zero quantity.

positives: I have no money because they cost £250.
I had no clothes to wear at John's party.
negatives: No, I don't want to go.
There is a no smoking sign.

guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS POSTMODIFIER
can_do_statement: Can post-modify noun phrases by using a non-defining relative clause. ► Clauses: relative

ontology.mental_model: Adding supplementary details to an entity using a clause that does not restrict its identity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a comma and 'which', 'who', or 'whose' to give extra information about a noun.

positives: He played for the other team, which lost.
I saw John, who is my brother.
negatives: The car which I bought is red.
I do not know who she is.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying nouns with an increasing range of determiners.

ontology.mental_model: Specifying quantities or identities of entities using a broader set of determining words.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using quantifiers like 'many', 'much', 'some', 'all', or 'a lot of' before a noun.

positives: There are so many shops here.
I had so much fun today.
negatives: Many of the shops are closed.
Much to my surprise, he left.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Pointing out mass entities that cannot be counted individually.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using determiners like 'the', 'some', or 'more' with words for substances or concepts.

positives: The food was delicious.
I need to do some homework.
negatives: I ate an apple.
There is a lot of cars.

can_do_statement: Can pre-modify noun phrases with a limited range of more than one adjective.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using two or more adjectives in a row before a noun.

positives: I bought a beautiful pink skirt.
She has short black hair.
negatives: I bought a pink skirt.
The shirt is beautiful and pink.

guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS COMPLEMENT
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases by using a defining relative clause as a complement to a noun phrase. ► Clauses: relative

ontology.mental_model: Restricting the identity of an entity using a clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which', 'who', 'that', or 'when' right after a noun without a comma.

positives: The mobile phone which I bought is brilliant.
The person who gave me it was my father.
negatives: The mobile phone, which I bought yesterday, is brilliant.
I know who did it.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiner ''s' with a singular noun.

ontology.mental_model: Indicating ownership or association of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using apostrophe S ('s) attached to a noun to show possession.

positives: It is my sister's jacket.
I saw my neighbour's car.
negatives: He's going to the store.
It's a beautiful day.

can_do_statement: Can use the '-ing' forms of verbs as nouns, in object position, to refer to activities.

ontology.mental_model: Activity conceptualized as an entity receiving the verb's action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using the -ing form as an object of another verb like 'like' or 'prefer'.

positives: I prefer dancing.
I really enjoy swimming.
negatives: I am dancing.
She prefers the book.

can_do_statement: Can form plurals of countable nouns ending in a consonant plus '-y', by changing the 'y' to 'I' and adding '-es'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Spelling rule: changing y to i and adding es.

positives: I have a lot of hobbies.
There were many activities.
negatives: He lies to me.
She tries hard.

can_do_statement: Can form plurals by adding '-es' to countable nouns ending in '-o', '-ch', '-s', '-sh', '-x' or '-z'.

ontology.mental_model: Multiplicity of entities requiring an extra syllable or vowel sound for pronunciation
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Spelling rule: adding es to specific noun endings.

positives: The art classes are fun.
I bought five dresses.
negatives: He goes home.
She teaches math.

can_do_statement: Can form some irregular plural nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Irregular plural nouns that don't end in s.

positives: I bought some clothes for my children.
She has nice teeth.
negatives: The child is happy.
My tooth hurts.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of uncountable nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Talking about things you can't count, like music, weather, and money.

positives: I listen to music, I watch TV and I talk to my friends.
Bring some money with you.
negatives: The cat is black.
She likes cars.

guideword: FORM: NOUNS ONLY USED IN THE PLURAL
can_do_statement: Can use nouns that only have a plural form, with plural agreement.

ontology.mental_model: Objects naturally consisting of pairs or multiples treated as grammatically plural
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Plural-only nouns and their verb agreement.

positives: The clothes are very cheap.
My glasses were expensive.
negatives: I bought some new clothes.
I wear glasses.

can_do_statement: Can use uncountable nouns with 'the' to talk about something specific.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the' to talk about a specific amount or instance of an uncountable noun.

positives: The music is going to be loud, since it's rap.
If you can't find the information about the new art class after school, please call me.
negatives: The cat is black.
I like the apples.

can_do_statement: Can use uncountable nouns with a limited range of quantity words and phrases including 'some', 'any', 'a lot of', 'more'. ► Determiners: quantity

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'some', 'any', 'a lot of', or 'more' with uncountable nouns.

positives: I need to do some homework.
We have had a lot of fun.
negatives: I have some apples.
I need more chairs.

can_do_statement: Can refer to an individual example or quantity of an uncountable noun using words for containers and countable items.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using countable containers (like a bottle or a piece) for uncountable things.

positives: We have to bring a bottle of water, trainers and a T-shirt or top.
I can drink a cup of tea in a café.
negatives: I like water.
He drank tea.

can_do_statement: Can use the past simple passive affirmative after a singular subject.

ontology.mental_model: Past state or action received by singular subject.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Singular past simple passive.

positives: The letter was written in pencil.
I was told to wait here.
negatives: They were given a prize.
The house was not built yet.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple passive affirmative with a singular subject.

ontology.mental_model: Present state or characteristic received by a singular subject.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Singular present simple passive.

positives: The bag is made of leather.
It is called a spatula.
negatives: They are called heroes.
It is not known.

can_do_statement: Can use the passive with 'by' to add information about something already known.

ontology.mental_model: Identifying the agent of a passive action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Passive agent 'by'.

positives: The book was written by my friend.
It is made by a famous company.
negatives: I sat by the river.
We will travel by train.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past continuous affirmative.

positives: I was waiting for you all evening.
They were playing football.
negatives: Was I waiting for you?
I was not waiting for you.

can_do_statement: Can use the past continuous with a limited range of adverbs in the normal mid position.

ontology.mental_model: Modifying past ongoing action with simple adverb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past continuous + just/always.

positives: I was just watching a match.
She was always dreaming of it.
negatives: I was watching a match just now.
He was constantly bothering me.

can_do_statement: Can use the past continuous to show that an event was happening in the background to the main event.

ontology.mental_model: Background ongoing event interrupted by main event.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past continuous background + past simple main.

positives: It was raining when I arrived.
We were studying and I left my book.
negatives: I was studying all day long.
It rained when I arrived.

can_do_statement: Can use the past continuous to talk about actions and states in progress around a particular time in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Event anchored to specific past time.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past continuous with specific time reference.

positives: Yesterday I was watching a game.
We were sleeping at 10 PM.
negatives: I watched a game yesterday.
I will be sleeping at 10 PM.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple affirmative using regular or common irregular verbs.

positives: I forgot to tell you some details about tomorrow evening.
My favourite team won the championship.
negatives: I forget to tell you details.
My favourite team is winning.

can_do_statement: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'you' with a limited range of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Seeking information about a completed past action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming questions in the past using 'did' with the pronoun 'you'.

positives: Did you buy something yesterday?
When did you quickly find it?
negatives: Do you buy something yesterday?
Have you found it yet?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Stating that a past event did not happen.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'did not' or 'didn't' to form negative past statements.

positives: You did not keep your promise.
I didn't tell you that my house is opposite the cinema.
negatives: You do not keep your promise.
I haven't told you that my house is opposite.

can_do_statement: Can use 'when' + past simple in subordinate clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Setting a point in time when something else happened.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'when' before a past simple clause.

positives: When I arrived, the weather was horrible.
I left it in the kitchen when I completely fell down.
negatives: When I arrive, the weather is horrible.
I am leaving it in the kitchen when I fall.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'yet' to talk about events which are expected to be completed at some point in the future.

ontology.mental_model: Expectation of a completion in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negative present perfect simple with 'yet'

positives: I haven't finished my homework yet.
She has not seen the new movie yet.
negatives: I didn't see the movie yet.
I did not see that one.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'for' to talk about a past event or action which hasn't occurred again in the period of time up to now.

ontology.mental_model: Absence of an action over a period of time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negative present perfect simple with 'for'

positives: I haven't eaten pizza for a month.
We haven't met for ages.
negatives: I didn't see it yet.
I have lived here for a long time.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form 'have' + '-ed' with pronouns 'I' and 'we', and with a limited range of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting a past experience with present relevance
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Affirmative present perfect simple with I and We

positives: I have visited the museum several times.
We've completed the project.
negatives: They have been to the museum.
I hadn't seen the movie.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form 'haven't' + '-ed' with 'I' with a limited range of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Denying a past experience up to the present
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negative present perfect simple with 'I'

positives: I haven't tried Italian food.
I have not seen that episode.
negatives: We haven't been there.
He hasn't called me.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form 'have you' + '-ed' with with a limited range of verbs.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Question form 'have you' + past participle

positives: Have you finished your dinner?
Where have you been all day?
negatives: Have they seen the show?
Do you have a pet?

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple with a limited range of adverbs in the normal mid position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect simple with mid-position adverbs

positives: I have never visited the museum.
She has just left the building.
negatives: I have already seen it.
They haven't finished it.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple to talk about experiences up to now.

ontology.mental_model: Stating life experiences without a specific time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect simple for experiences

positives: I have visited the Coliseum.
She has never been to France.
negatives: I am going to the British Museum.
He went to the museum yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'just' to modify prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Adding precision or exactness to a spatial or temporal location.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Put 'just' before a preposition to mean 'exactly' or 'very close to'.

positives: It's just near the cinema.
My house is just after the library.
negatives: I just arrived.
He just called me.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of complex prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Multi-word phrases acting as single conceptual links.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Some prepositions are made of two or three words, like 'next to' or 'such as'.

positives: We can meet in the park near to my house.
I have a lot of hobbies, such as reading.
negatives: I am near the house.
The front door is open.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of simple (single-word) prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Expanding the set of spatial, temporal, and abstract relationships.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: You can use words like 'during', 'between', 'opposite', and 'by' to give more precise locations or times.

positives: Please return it by tomorrow morning.
The match was between Arsenal and Liverpool.
negatives: I am happy today.
She walks fast.

can_do_statement: Can form prepositional phrases using the '-ing' form of verbs as complements.

ontology.mental_model: Treating actions (verbs) as noun concepts following a relationship word.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When a verb comes immediately after a preposition (like 'by', 'about', 'for'), it must be in the '-ing' form.

positives: I can help by bringing the sound box.
I was crazy about playing tennis.
negatives: I like bringing my own lunch.
He started playing tennis yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can end a 'wh-' question with a preposition, where the preposition is stranded from its complement.

ontology.mental_model: Delaying the preposition until the end of a question where the object is the question word.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: In English, questions often end with the preposition, like 'Who are you talking to?'

positives: Who are you going with?
So what are you waiting for?
negatives: With whom are you going?
For what are you waiting?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Inserting 'not' between the 'be' auxiliary and the present participle.

positives: I am not using the computer anymore.
The fridge isn't working at the moment.
negatives: She wasn't looking at me yesterday.
I am eating a really big apple.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with an increasing range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using the continuous aspect with a wider set of dynamic verbs.

positives: I am watching a huge swimming competition.
It is getting warmer outside today.
negatives: I am doing my homework tonight.
She watches television almost every day.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about temporary situations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Highlighting a living, working, or studying arrangement as impermanent.

positives: I am living with my friend in the city.
I am studying hard at the new college.
negatives: I am going to the large public park.
She lives in a small apartment in London.

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-' questions, especially in the context of letters and emails.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Inverting the subject and auxiliary in present continuous WH- questions.

positives: How are you doing today?
What are you bringing with you to the party?
negatives: What do you do every day at work?
I am doing quite well today.

guideword: FORM/USE: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of adverbs of indefinite frequency, often to talk about surprising or undesirable situations or events (especially with 'always').

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present continuous with 'always' for habits

positives: I am always losing my keys.
She is always talking during the movie.
negatives: I always walk to school.
They are walking to the store now.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Present simple affirmative with diverse verbs
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic present simple statements

positives: They bring me good luck every day.
It takes about half an hour to get there.
negatives: They are bringing me good luck right now.
She took a long time to answer the phone.

guideword: FORM/USE: REAL AND IMAGINED SITUATIONS AFTER 'IF'
can_do_statement: Can use the present simple after 'if' to talk about real and imagined situations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: First conditional with present simple

positives: If you want some help, I will be free next week.
If he doesn't arrive soon, we will start without him.
negatives: I want some help with this project.
If he arrived earlier, we wouldn't be late.

guideword: FORM: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with adverbs of indefinite frequency.    ► adverbs

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Routines with frequency adverbs

positives: People usually try to eat their breakfast early.
They always make special things for their celebrations.
negatives: She usually went to the store before it closed.
I have always wanted to visit that museum.

can_do_statement: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'you'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple questions with 'you'

positives: Do you have a mobile phone?
What do you think about my mobile phone?
negatives: Did you go to the store?
Are you going to the concert?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with an increasing range of regular and irregular verbs.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple negative (don't/doesn't)

positives: I don't need the video because I've got the DVD.
It doesn't cost very much.
negatives: I didn't need the video.
He has not gone to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with a limited range of mental process verbs including 'think', 'hope', 'know'.

ontology.mental_model: Expression of thought, hope, or knowledge
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Mental process verbs (think, hope, know)

positives: I think my bag is in your kitchen.
Do you know that I am going to a concert on Saturday?
negatives: I am thinking about going to the store.
She hoped he would return.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with 'why don't you…?', 'Why don’t we…?' and 'if you want or if you like' to make suggestions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Suggestions with 'why don't' or 'if you like'

positives: Why don't you wear your black suit?
We can go there, if you like.
negatives: I don't know why you did that.
I wonder if you liked the movie.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple to give instructions and directions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Instructions and directions

positives: Then you turn right and my house is on your left.
Then you go straight on for about fifty meters.
negatives: I turned left at the corner.
We will cross the street.

can_do_statement: Can form indirect questions with 'Do you know' + 'how', 'where', 'why', or 'what …?'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Indirect questions with 'Do you know'

positives: Do you know how to get to my house?
Do you know what time it is?
negatives: Do you know him well?
Did you know how to get there?

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'of' in the phrases 'a friend of mine' and 'friends of mine'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'of mine' instead of 'my' for emphasis or variation.

positives: A friend of mine gave me this book.
I saw some friends of mine yesterday.
negatives: My friend gave me this book.
That book is mine.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours', with singular reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'yours' instead of 'your + noun' as an object or complement.

positives: I also loved yours.
It's like yours.
negatives: Yours is better.
Yours looks nice.

can_do_statement: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine', with singular and plural reference, in subject and object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: First-person singular possession as an independent entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'mine' as a standalone pronoun in various positions.

positives: The phone is not mine.
Mine are too small for me.
negatives: It is a gold mine.
He works in a coal mine.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of singular reflexive pronouns ('myself', 'yourself') with a limited range of verbs ('enjoy', 'buy') to refer to actions where the subject and object of the verb are the same.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'myself' or 'yourself' with 'enjoy' or 'buy'

positives: I enjoyed myself so much at the party.
I bought myself a yellow T-shirt.
negatives: She enjoyed herself at the beach.
I bought a shirt for myself.

can_do_statement: Can leave out the subject pronoun with 'hope'. ► ellipsis

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Sounding natural and friendly

positives: Hope to see you soon.
Hope you feel better.
negatives: Hope is what keeps us going.
I hope to win.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it' as an empty subject when there is nothing else to put in subject position, particularly with weather or time.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Talking about the weather or time

positives: It's cold outside.
I think it is 5 o'clock.
negatives: It is my book.
It is a cat.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' as a pronoun with singular reference.

ontology.mental_model: Using a singular demonstrative pronoun to refer to a nearby or salient entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'This' as a standalone pronoun.

positives: This is exactly what I wanted.
I cannot believe you did this.
negatives: This car is too fast for me.
I will go this morning.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to refer back to single things or groups of plural things which have already been mentioned.

ontology.mental_model: Using 'this' anaphorically to summarize or reference a prior noun phrase.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'This' referring back.

positives: Thank you so much for this.
I never asked for all this.
negatives: This book belongs to me.
This man came to my house.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to point to or identify single things or entities which are about to follow and have immediate relevance.

ontology.mental_model: Cataphoric or deictic reference using 'this' before revealing the entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'This' pointing forward.

positives: This is my phone number if you need it.
This is the information you requested.
negatives: This computer is completely broken.
He bought this house last year.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' as a pronoun to refer back to something which has already been mentioned.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'That' referring back.

positives: I really didn't know about that.
We will deal with that later.
negatives: That dog is very loud.
I think that he is right.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that's' + adjective to respond to something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'That's' + adjective.

positives: That's wonderful news!
That's great to hear!
negatives: That dog is absolutely great.
I think that is it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that' as a pronoun with singular reference.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'That' as a singular pronoun.

positives: That was a really amazing show.
I can't believe he said that.
negatives: I know that you are lying.
That man is my uncle.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to refer to something that is happening now.

ontology.mental_model: Using 'this' to refer to a current, ongoing experience.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'This' for the present moment.

positives: This is the best party ever!
This is turning into a huge disaster.
negatives: I will do this tomorrow morning.
This old picture reminds me of you.

can_do_statement: Can use 'that's all' to end a letter.

ontology.mental_model: Summarizing the entirety of a message to signal closing.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'That's all' to sign off.

positives: Well, I guess that's all for now.
Anyway, that's all from me.
negatives: That's all the money I have.
Is that all you can say?

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of pronouns ('all', 'both') with 'of' followed by an object pronoun, to refer to quantity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: referring to the entirety or duality of a specific group using 'all/both of'

positives: All of them went to the park.
I invited both of us to the party.
negatives: All the people went there.
Both sisters are coming.

can_do_statement: Can use pronouns 'some' and 'any', to refer to quantity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: using 'some' and 'any' independently to refer back to quantities without nouns

positives: I need some.
They don't have any.
negatives: I need some water.
Any person can do this.

can_do_statement: Can use 'some' as a subject and object to refer back to a plural or uncountable noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: using 'some' independently to refer to a previously mentioned noun

positives: Some were playing outside.
You can bring some.
negatives: Some people were there.
I read some books.

can_do_statement: Can use 'any' as an object in a negative clause to refer back to a plural or uncountable noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: using 'any' as an object in negative contexts

positives: I don't have any.
She did not see any.
negatives: I don't have any apples.
Has anyone seen any?

can_do_statement: Can use 'one' as a pronoun to substitute for singular countable nouns which have already been mentioned or are obvious from the context.

ontology.mental_model: Pronoun substitution for a singular noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'one' instead of repeating a noun

positives: I bought a new pullover, because my old one is too small.
I chose the black one with the numbers in orange.
negatives: I have one dog.
One day I will go there.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the one' and 'the' + pre-modifier + 'one' with a complement, to refer to something specific.

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a particular item using 'the one' with a postmodifier
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'the one with/who/that' to be specific

positives: My house is No.8 and it's the one with silver gates.
Do you remember the one that we saw last week?
negatives: I have one.
He was the one.

can_do_statement: Can use determiners + premodifers + 'one'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using words like 'a new one' or 'the blue one'

positives: I love blue so I bought the blue one.
I like my present very much because I needed a new one.
negatives: He has one car.
I need one right now.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns as objects or complements of prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Referring to an unspecified entity as an object of a verb or preposition
ontology.pedagogical_hook: indefinite pronoun as object

positives: I need it because I have to call someone.
I have borrowed it from somebody.
negatives: Someone left their bag here.
Everyone knows that the earth is round.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of indefinite pronouns ('someone', 'everyone') as subjects, with a singular verb.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: someone/everyone as subject

positives: I bought them because someone stole my luggage at the airport.
When someone calls me, it rings with a lovely song.
negatives: I didn't invite someone else to the party.
She asked everyone to join the meeting.

can_do_statement: Can use 'something' in vague expressions, to refer to things in a non-specific way.

ontology.mental_model: Vague extension of a category or choice
ontology.pedagogical_hook: or something (like that/else)

positives: After the concert we can have a pizza or something else.
You can bring a cake or something like that.
negatives: I really need to eat something.
Something bad happened yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can modify 'something' or 'anything' with an adjective, to make it more specific.

ontology.mental_model: Post-modification of an unspecified entity to restrict its scope
ontology.pedagogical_hook: something/anything + adjective

positives: Next weekend it's my mum's birthday party, so I needed something new to wear.
You don't have to bring anything special.
negatives: I need something else to read.
Something feels completely wrong about this.

can_do_statement: Can use 'anything' after a negative verb form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'anything' instead of 'something' after negative verbs.

positives: I don't have anything to wear.
She hasn't seen anything.
negatives: I have anything you need.
Do you have anything?

can_do_statement: Can use indefinite pronouns with 'else'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'else' to mean 'other' or 'additional'.

positives: Do you need anything else?
I have someone else in mind.
negatives: I need something else's cover.
Who else is coming?

can_do_statement: Can modify 'something' or 'anything' with 'to' infinitive, to make it more specific.

ontology.mental_model: Specifying purpose for an indefinite entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Adding an infinitive verb to explain what the 'something' or 'anything' is for.

positives: I need something to drink.
Do you have anything to say?
negatives: I gave something to him.
She sent anything to the wrong address.

can_do_statement: Can use 'you' to refer to people in general.

ontology.mental_model: Generalization of the human subject using the second person
ontology.pedagogical_hook: informal generic 'you'

positives: With a good phone, you can play games.
If you want to travel to China, you need to learn a little Chinese.
negatives: Did you take my book?
I want to tell you a secret.

can_do_statement: Can form alternative questions with two words from the same class combined with 'or'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Connecting parallel words with 'or'

positives: Is it cheap or expensive for you?
Can you bring some food or drinks for the dinner?
negatives: Do you want this one, or the other one?
Is it in the car or on the table?

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of question tags.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using simple question tags for agreement

positives: It differs from the story which you told me, doesn't it?
It's fantastic, isn't it?
negatives: You'll see the programme on the 23rd, won't you?
We could go on holiday together, couldn't we?

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'have' to form 'wh-'questions. ► present perfect  ►  past perfect

ontology.mental_model: Questioning state/actions connected to the present using perfect aspect
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask questions about past experiences or recent events using 'wh-' words and 'have'
ontology.agency_or_distance: High agency, inquiring for specific information

positives: What have you brought for me?
How have you been lately?
negatives: I know what you have done.
Who has the keys?

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions. ► present simple;  ► past simple

ontology.mental_model: Seeking factual information or opinions in simple aspects
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask questions in the present or past simple using 'wh-' words and 'do'

positives: What do you think about it?
Where did you go yesterday?
negatives: I don't know what to do.
Tell me how you do it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'be' to form 'wh-'questions. ► present continuous ► past continuous

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about ongoing or planned actions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask questions about continuous actions or plans using 'wh-' words and 'be'
ontology.agency_or_distance: High agency, gathering information on events in progress

positives: Where are you going tonight?
Who were they talking to?
negatives: I asked who she was.
What is the answer?

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-'words + modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions.

ontology.mental_model: Questioning possibilities, abilities, or future intentions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask questions involving modals for future plans, ability, or permission
ontology.agency_or_distance: High agency, exploring options or asking for help

positives: What will you bring to the party?
How can I help you today?
negatives: I wonder what she will say.
Tell me how I can help.

can_do_statement: Can use negative question 'why don’t' + pronoun + verb, to make a suggestion or invitation.

ontology.mental_model: Proposing a shared action or suggesting a course of action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To suggest or invite someone to do something using 'Why don't we/you'

positives: Why don't we watch a film tonight?
Why don't you come with me?
negatives: Why don't they listen?
I asked him why you don't care.

can_do_statement: Can use 'wh-'words + main verb 'be' + subject to form 'wh-' questions.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about states, descriptions, or locations
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask about facts or current states using 'wh-' words and the verb 'be'

positives: How was your dinner yesterday?
Where are you now?
negatives: I wonder where you are.
What are you doing today?

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary 'be' + subject + the '-ing' form (continuous form) to form 'yes/no' questions.

ontology.mental_model: Asking for verification about ongoing or future planned actions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To ask yes/no questions in the continuous aspect using 'be' + '-ing'
ontology.agency_or_distance: High agency, confirming current or future events

positives: Are you feeling better?
Are you doing anything on Friday?
negatives: I am wondering if you are going.
She is working right now.

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using do to ask a yes/no question

positives: Do you want some tea, John?
Did he go to the store?
negatives: I do not want any tea.
They did not do it.

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary 'have' + subject + the '-ed' form to form 'yes/no' questions.  ►  present perfect

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using have to ask a yes/no question

positives: Have you seen this movie, buddy?
Has she arrived yet?
negatives: I have a car.
They have gone away.

can_do_statement: Can use main verb 'be' + subject to form 'yes/no' questions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using be to ask a yes/no question

positives: Are you ready for the test, kids?
Is this the right train?
negatives: I am ready.
You are here.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a modal to ask a yes/no question

positives: Can you help me with this, please?
Would you like some coffee?
negatives: I can help you.
They would be happy.

guideword: FORM: REPORTED STATEMENTS WITH 'SAY', PRONOUN SHIFT
can_do_statement: Can report statements using a reporting clause with 'say' + 'that-'clause, with a pronoun shift where relevant.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using say to report statements

positives: She says that she was happy.
They said that it was a good idea.
negatives: She said something.
I heard that she said it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'look forward to' as a fixed expression followed by an '-ing' form or noun phrase, usually at the end of correspondence.

ontology.mental_model: Anticipating a future event with pleasure.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'look forward to' before an -ing verb or noun.

positives: I am looking forward to seeing you!
I look forward to our meeting.
negatives: I look forward.
Look forward and walk.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs, typically reporting, with a 'that'-clause as the direct object.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting thoughts or statements using a reporting verb followed by an explicit 'that' clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'that' to introduce a reported statement.

positives: I hope that you'll come.
My mother said that she can help us.
negatives: I hope you'll come.
He pointed at the book that was on the table.

can_do_statement: Can use verbs, typically reporting verbs, followed by a noun or pronoun as the indirect object and a clause with or without 'that', as the direct object.

ontology.mental_model: Relaying messages or commitments directed at specific individuals
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To report what someone communicated to someone else using an indirect object and a clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Medium agency, mediating information transfer between parties

positives: I told you that she has a new car.
Nisha told me you had an accident last week.
negatives: I told the story to her.
She promised to help me later.

guideword: FORM: VERBS + DIRECT OBJECT CLAUSE WITHOUT 'THAT'
can_do_statement: Can use reporting verbs, especially mental process verbs, with a clause as the direct object, without 'that', especially in informal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing informal thoughts, beliefs, or statements directly
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To informally state beliefs or reports without using the word 'that'
ontology.agency_or_distance: High agency, direct expression of cognitive state

positives: I think you should go visit the towers.
I hope you can go with us.
negatives: I think that you should go.
I hope for the best.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs without an object.

ontology.mental_model: Describing actions that are self-contained without affecting external entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a phrasal verb that doesn't need an object.

positives: I'm going to get up early.
We can meet up at 2 pm.
negatives: I get up the stairs.
I wake him up.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.

ontology.mental_model: Manipulating specific entities with common phrasal verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting a pronoun in the middle of a simple phrasal verb.

positives: I will pick you up tomorrow.
Ring me up if you have questions.
negatives: I will pick up the bag.
Ring up the manager.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of modal auxiliary verbs.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a wider range of modals like should and might

positives: I think we should go somewhere else.
They might get dirty.
negatives: I will go somewhere else.
I can play the piano.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verbs with adjective complements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using linking verbs other than be

positives: The room looks bigger with the new color.
The color blue always looks fresh.
negatives: I look at the sky every night.
We will look into the matter.

can_do_statement: Can use auxiliary verbs 'have' and 'do'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using have and do as auxiliaries

positives: I have left my suitcase in your house.
Do you like shopping online?
negatives: I have a big suitcase.
I did the homework yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verb 'have (got) to'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using have got to or have to

positives: You've got to bring paintbrushes.
You don't have to bring anything.
negatives: I have a lot of things to do.
She has got a new car to drive.

can_do_statement: Can use verbs expressing preference followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.

ontology.mental_model: expressing strong preferences with interchangeable forms
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs of preference (love, hate, prefer) + to/ing

positives: I love to sing in the shower.
She hates waiting for the bus.
negatives: I love the beautiful flowers.
I hate the bus.

can_do_statement: Can use 'enjoy' followed by the '-ing' form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: enjoy + ing

positives: I enjoy reading books at night.
She enjoys playing tennis.
negatives: I enjoy the beautiful morning.
He enjoys a good book.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would love to' followed by the 'to'-infinitive to give emphasis.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: would love to + infinitive

positives: I would love to see you tomorrow.
I'd really love to come along.
negatives: I love to see you tomorrow.
I would like to come along.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of verbs followed by a 'to'-infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: expanding repertoire of verbs taking infinitives
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs (remember, forget, decide, plan) + to infinitive

positives: I forgot to call my mother.
They decided not to stay.
negatives: I forgot my mother's number.
They planned a huge party.

can_do_statement: Can use 'there is' + uncountable nouns as complement.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Uncountable nouns use singular 'there is'.

positives: I need it because there is some money in it.
There is some information about the new art class.
negatives: There is a dog sleeping on the floor.
There's a lot of people here.

can_do_statement: Can use both 'there is' and 'there are' + 'a lot of' + plural noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'a lot of' to state there is a large quantity of something.

positives: There's a lot of people there.
You can go to the town centre because there are a lot of shops.
negatives: There are many people standing around.
There is one person who can help.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of linking verbs with complements.

ontology.mental_model: Using an increasing range of linking verbs (look, become, get, feel) with adjectival complements.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using linking verbs to talk about changes or feelings.

positives: It looks good on you.
Make sure they won't get dirty.
negatives: He looked at the picture.
I got a new car.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to make requests in a limited range of contexts.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking for things

positives: Will you come with me?
Will you be able to visit some museums with me?
negatives: I will come with you.
Where will you go?

guideword: FORM: COMBINING MORE THAN TWO ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can use commas and 'and' to join more than two adjectives, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: list of attributes closed by and
ontology.pedagogical_hook: list them, then close the list

positives: The car is big, fast and beautiful.
They are very smart, funny and kind.
negatives: The car is big and fast.
There is a big, fast and beautiful car.

guideword: FORM: COMBINING THE SAME COMPARATIVE ADJECTIVE WITH 'AND'
can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to repeat a comparative adjective to indicate change over time, usually after 'become' or get. ► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the change keeps changing

positives: The weather became hotter and hotter.
They are getting better and better.
negatives: The city was growing and growing.
I was taking vitamins and this and this.

can_do_statement: Can use a comma to combine two adjectives used before the noun, following the usual order of adjective types.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: load the noun

positives: It is a small, quiet town.
She has a beautiful, old house.
negatives: Hello, Aaron, nice to meet you.
It was a small issue, bad for us.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of compound adjectives ('good-looking', 'well-known')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen joins two roots into one trait
ontology.pedagogical_hook: two roots, one trait

positives: He is a very good-looking man.
She is a well-known writer.
negatives: I am watching Spider-Man.
We need high performance.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of comparative adjectives.► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.pedagogical_hook: more of both

positives: Computers are getting cheaper and better.
The weather is warmer and nicer today.
negatives: It is cheaper, and the quality is better.
The weather is hot and humid.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to repeat a comparative adjective to indicate change over time, usually after 'become' or 'get'.  ► adjectives: comparatives

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the change keeps changing

positives: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.
My English is becoming better and better.
negatives: It was growing and growing.
We bought tons and tons of it.

can_do_statement: Can use '(so) much' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: much stretches the distance between two scale points
ontology.pedagogical_hook: widen the gap

positives: It is much better now.
The car was so much bigger.
negatives: I remember they were much better players.
He runs much better today.

can_do_statement: Can use 'a (little) bit' to modify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: a bit narrows the distance between scale points
ontology.pedagogical_hook: shrink the gap politely

positives: It is a bit bigger now.
The room was a little bit better.
negatives: Yeah, can you make it a bit bigger?
He spoke a bit faster.

can_do_statement: Can use 'even' to modify and intensify comparative adjectives used predicatively after a verb, usually 'be' and 'get'.

ontology.mental_model: even pushes an already high point higher
ontology.pedagogical_hook: climb one rung more

positives: It is even better today.
The weather got even hotter.
negatives: They just have even better players.
We have even cheaper prices.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' before adjectives followed by 'to'-infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: excess degree slams the door on the action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: too much, so it can't happen

positives: He is too young to drive.
The car was too expensive to buy.
negatives: It was too long to read.
It is too dangerous to release.

can_do_statement: Can use 'enough' to modify adjectives.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: past the line

positives: The house is big enough for us.
My coffee is not strong enough.
negatives: Enough has been said about it.
We have enough big boxes.

can_do_statement: Can use adjective phrases attributively, before a noun.

ontology.mental_model: intensifier plus adjective packed before the noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: stack it before the noun

positives: It was a really difficult situation for us.
She is a very good person.
negatives: They are very difficult to move.
The exam was very difficult I think.

can_do_statement: Can form adjective phrases with 'quite a' + adjective.

ontology.mental_model: quite a lifts the whole noun phrase a notch
ontology.pedagogical_hook: quite a step up

negatives: The answer is quite clear.
She was quite happy alone.
positives: I have been thinking about it for quite a long time.
This is quite a difficult situation you have.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives with the prefix a- ('asleep', 'awake', 'alive', 'alone') predicatively only, after linking verbs.

ontology.mental_model: a- adjectives are states, never glued before nouns
ontology.pedagogical_hook: a- words stay after the verb

positives: The baby is currently asleep.
I feel completely alone right now.
negatives: He is afraid of the large spiders.
The awake baby cried all night long.

can_do_statement:
Can use an increasing range of adjectives attributively, before a noun.
► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: several attributes stack inside the noun phrase
ontology.pedagogical_hook: stack them in order

negatives: The character is main to the plot.
Her hair is long and dark.
positives: The main character in the programme is a journalist.
He had long dark hair and a short fair beard.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives as object complement after 'make'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: make + object + adjective — name the result state of the action on the entity
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker attributes the resulting state to a caused entity

positives: It makes me happy.
She made the room clean.
negatives: I make a fast read.
We make some viral videos.

can_do_statement: Can use an adjective or adjective phrase after pronouns like 'something', 'nothing', 'somewhere', 'nowhere'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: something / nothing + adjective — leave the referent vague and color it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker keeps the referent indeterminate while coloring it

positives: I want to show you something really interesting.
He gave me nothing useful today.
negatives: I saw something like a ghost in the dark.
He knew someone who was very rich.

can_do_statement: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with a superlative adjective + prepositional phrase, to talk about something unique. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Situating a superlative within a defined scope or domain via prepositions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Forming complex superlative noun phrases for precise uniqueness

positives: Yesterday was the most exciting day of my life!
Exercise is undoubtedly the most important thing in our lives.
negatives: It is the best.
It was a very exciting day of my life.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'THE BEST' WITH NOUN AND PRESENT PERFECT
can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' before a noun + present perfect to talk about a unique experience.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the best + noun + have ever + past participle — name a unique experience up to speech time
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker locates the unique experience at the open-ended present

positives: It's the best meal I have ever eaten.
That was the best trip we have ever taken.
negatives: It was the best meal yesterday.
The best thing about her is her honesty.

guideword: FORM: 'THE BEST' WITH NOUN AND  'TO-' INFINITIVE
can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' before a noun + 'to'-infinitive.  ► clauses: comparative

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the best + noun + to + verb — name the top context for an action
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions an action as the top-of-its-kind purpose

positives: It is the best book to read.
This is the best computer to buy.
negatives: He is the best to play the game.
She sent the best procedure to the operation.

can_do_statement: Can use 'one of the' before a superlative adjective, followed by a plural noun. ► noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Positioning an entity within a top-tier group rather than as an absolute singular
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'one of the' for inclusive superlatives

positives: It was one of the best days of my life.
Akihabara is one of the most famous places in Tokyo.
negatives: It is the best day.
I have one of the tickets.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with a range of determiners before a superlative adjective. ► noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: determiner + superlative + noun — slot any determiner before the rank
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker frames the top rank against any context

positives: He is my best friend in the world.
That was their most important decision.
negatives: He is the best friend you can have.
They like most important things in life.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: recently / immediately / eventually / finally — finer time-pointers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pinpoints the event on a more granular S-anchored line

positives: I went to the cinema with a new friend recently.
I immediately called her to see if everything was OK.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She spoke to her mother.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of manner adverbs and adverb phrases to modify how something happens.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: carefully / gradually / properly — wider texture palette for the verb's HOW
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker expands the texture vocabulary of the action

positives: She walked slowly.
Find ways to operate safely.
negatives: Fully of work.
It is highly likely.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('near', 'far away', 'upstairs', 'downstairs') to indicate place.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: near / far away / upstairs / downstairs — place the event on the spatial stage
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions entities in shared physical space

positives: They are upstairs.
She lives far away.
negatives: I live near the station.
There was a factory near my born town.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use 'really really' with verbs and adjectives for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Adverb doubling signals intensification through repetition, creating a cumulative emphatic effect that amplifies the degree adverb's semantic contribution.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Double 'really' as emphatic intensifier — the learner exploits English adverb morphology by repetition to convey heightened intensity, a productive strategy even at intermediate levels.
ontology.agency_or_distance: SENDER_HIGH — the doubled form reflects the speaker's strong personal commitment to the proposition.

positives: I really really like her smile.
It was really really boring.
negatives: I really like it and I really mean it.
Really, really, is that true?

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs ('a little', 'a bit') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity. ► determiners

ontology.pedagogical_hook: a little / a bit — small step up from zero on the verb’s intensity dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker softens the verb’s force without abandoning it

positives: He smiled a little.
I understand it a bit!
negatives: I have a little money in my wallet.
Just a little piece, please.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('therefore', 'furthermore', 'otherwise') to show a relationship between two clauses or sentences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: therefore / furthermore / otherwise — wire two clauses with a logical link
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker binds clauses into consequence or addition

positives: I was sick; therefore, I stayed home.
It is raining, and furthermore, the wind is cold.
negatives: The difficulty therefore is high.
Additionally to the Pope, there are churches.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of focusing adverbs ('particularly', 'especially') to point to or highlight something. ► adverbs: position

ontology.pedagogical_hook: particularly / especially — spotlight one element from a presumed set
