ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent above others

positives: I like all animals, especially dogs.
The weather is particularly bad today.
negatives: He is a very special person.
She is particular about her food choices.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs as discourse markers to organise text.  ►  adverbs: position ►  Discourse markers

ontology.pedagogical_hook: firstly / secondly / furthermore / moreover — map discourse onto ordered slots
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker arranges the text in linear progression

positives: Firstly, I advise you to visit both schools.
Secondly, consider the long-term effects.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
She finished her homework.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('completely', 'obviously', 'clearly', 'actually', 'luckily', 'honestly', 'sadly', 'basically', 'obviously', 'hopefully') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / obviously / clearly / actually / luckily / honestly — dial the speaker's stance up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker takes explicit ownership of the stance

positives: But actually, he did not come to the party.
Hopefully, it will not rain tomorrow.
negatives: The story was obviously fake.
The water is clearly blue.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — calibrate certainty at finer resolution
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: I will probably go to the beach.
He is definitely coming to the party.
negatives: Maybe I will go to the store.
Perhaps he is coming later.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of manner adverbs to modify verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Describing the specific way an action is performed
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Add '-ly' words like 'carefully' or 'slowly' right next to the verb.

positives: You have to choose carefully.
She looked at me seriously and said something.
negatives: It is a carefully chosen gift.
That is a seriously bad idea.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of degree adverbs to modify adverbs. ► adverb phrases: form

ontology.mental_model: Intensifying the manner or timing of an action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combine words like 'really' and 'early' or 'very' and 'carefully'.

positives: We left really early on a Friday morning.
I opened it very carefully.
negatives: I am very happy.
It was a really good movie.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs to modify clauses and sentences to indicate stance or attitude.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing speaker attitude over an entire proposition
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a sentence with 'Luckily' or 'Obviously' to show how you feel about the whole statement.

positives: Obviously, you prefer going with your friends.
Luckily, I arrived in time.
negatives: He was obviously upset.
She luckily found her keys.

can_do_statement: Can modify an increasing range of adverbs with other adverbs.► adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings

ontology.mental_model: Modulating the intensity or precision of adverbs
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using adverbs to modify other adverbs for greater nuance

positives: We get along quite well.
It came out just yesterday.
negatives: We get along well.
It came out yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use 'than' + a finite clause forming the second part of a comparison after a comparative adjective

ontology.mental_model: Comparing against a state of affairs
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing reality to expectations or facts

positives: I wish our schools could become better than they are.
The room seems to be bigger than it is really.
negatives: He is taller than his brother.
It costs more than ten dollars.

can_do_statement: Can use 'than' + a limited range of non-finite clauses (with -ing), forming the second part of a comparison after a comparative adjective

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Comparing two activities directly

positives: It's less complicated than going to a large school in a town.
It will be more fun than sitting at home.
negatives: I have more money than the king.
He ran faster than he ever had before.

can_do_statement: Can use 'rather than' + noun phrase or prepositional phrase to stress one element in a comparison.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Expressing preference between two distinct entities

positives: Use the stairs rather than the lift.
Eat healthy foods rather than fatty foods.
negatives: I would rather go home than stay here.
He decided to resign rather than face dismissal.

can_do_statement: Can use '(not) as' + adjective/adverb + 'as' to introduce a clause (often with a substitute auxiliary verb) to talk about two things being equal or unequal in some way.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Equating attributes with actions

positives: I will try to cover the work as much as I can.
I'm not watching T.V. as often as I did.
negatives: It is as cold as ice.
He is as tall as his father.

can_do_statement: Can use 'too' + adjective + 'to'-infinitive.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Excess attribute preventing an action

positives: I think you are too young to go on holiday by yourself.
He always told me that he was too busy to write a letter to me.
negatives: I am going to the store too.
There are too many people here.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the best (that)' followed by a clause with the present perfect to talk about something unique.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Highest praise tied to experience

positives: It's the best place that I have ever seen.
Well, the best decision I've ever made was the decision to go to France.
negatives: He is the best player on the team.
I think this is the best one.

guideword: FORM: 'THE SAME' (+ NOUN) + 'AS' + PRONOUN OR NOUN
can_do_statement: Can use 'the same' (+ noun) + 'as' + pronoun or noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Stating identical properties between entities

positives: I wasn't the only one in my class, there were many others at the same level as me.
You like the same things as your friends.
negatives: I will do the same as I did before.
He arrived at the same time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so' + adjective + 'that' clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Degree so extreme it triggers an event

positives: I was so tired that I didn't have the strength to stand up.
I was so nervous that when the teacher talked to me, I shouted!
negatives: I did it so that you could be happy.
It is so cold today.

guideword: FORM: SENSE VERBS + 'AS IF' OR 'AS THOUGH' + FINITE CLAUSE
can_do_statement: Can use verbs of the senses + 'as if' or 'as though' + finite clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Projecting an unreal scenario based on feeling

positives: I was excited and I felt as if I was a bird.
I think I will have to buy an umbrella because it looks as if it'll rain.
negatives: He acted as if he owned the place.
It seems as though they forgot about us.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verbs + 'like' or 'similar to'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Describing objects by their similarity to others

positives: It smelled like roses.
Your story is similar to my last dream.
negatives: I like roses very much.
They have similar tastes.

guideword: FORM: COMBINING CLAUSES OF THE SAME TYPE
can_do_statement: Can combine clauses of the same type, main or subordinate, finite or non-finite, with conjunctions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using conjunctions for parallel structures

positives: They chose it because it is modern and there are many students.
You will have a great time because they are going to the seaside and they are staying in a hotel.
negatives: I am happy because I won.
He came and went.

can_do_statement: Can combine multiple main clauses with a range of conjunctions, often in a narrative context.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Telling a story with multiple events

positives: He was lost, so he went home, but then he found it.
I saw her, and I waved, so she smiled.
negatives: I like apples, oranges, and bananas.
He is tall and strong.

can_do_statement: Can combine two main clauses of the same type using 'either' in front or mid position, followed by 'or' to introduce the second clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Giving two choices

positives: You can either visit us or write to us.
Either I talk to her now or I will never talk to her.
negatives: I don't want either of them.
Do you want tea or coffee?

can_do_statement: Can use the auxiliary verb 'do' in an affirmative declarative clause, for emphasis and affirmation.

ontology.mental_model: Reaffirming or insisting on a fact
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Emphatic do

positives: Yes, I do have a favorite restaurant.
I do miss you.
negatives: Do you miss me?
I don't miss you.

can_do_statement: Can use 'do' + base form of a main verb, for emphasis or in formal contexts.

positives: Do sit down and relax for a moment.
Please do tell me the truth about what happened.
negatives: Do vacation or make vacation?
Do a podcast with this scientist.

can_do_statement: Can use the imperative to make an offer or an invitation.

positives: Come and stay with us this weekend!
Come visit us after the holidays.
negatives: They come and visit us every summer.
Come here right now please.

can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with 'let me' + base form of a main verb, as a focusing device, to introduce something

positives: Okay, let me check the schedule.
So, let me explain it to you.
negatives: He let me go early.
She didn't let me pay.

can_do_statement: Can form questions with a 'wh-' word as subject, without an auxiliary verb.

ontology.mental_model: Seeking the identity of the subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Wh- subject questions

positives: What happened?
Who cares?
negatives: What did you do?
Who is he?

can_do_statement: Can form interrogative clauses with an adverb in mid position, between the subject and the main verb.

ontology.mental_model: Asking about frequency or exact timing
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Questions with adverbs

positives: Have you ever been to Marseille?
Do you still remember my best friend?
negatives: Have you been to Marseille?
Don't you ever listen?

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Questions with which or whose

positives: Which book is yours?
Whose car are we taking?
negatives: Which is better?
I know whose it is.

can_do_statement: Can use 'How' + adjective.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing an intense emotional reaction to a situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'how' with an adjective for exclamation.

positives: How wonderful!
How strange.
negatives: How are you?
I don't know how fast he was going.

can_do_statement: Can use 'How' + adjective + clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing feeling regarding an entire clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'how' + adjective + clause.

positives: How lucky you are to have visited that exhibition!
How lovely to get your letter.
negatives: How exciting!
How do you do that?

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses, 'the person who/that, the thing that, the (only) one who/that' as a focusing device.

ontology.mental_model: Focusing attention on a specific entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the thing that' or 'the person who' to emphasize a particular subject
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency in structuring information for emphasis

positives: The thing that was great is the weather.
The person who sat next to me was her.
negatives: A person who does that is bad.
The thing was that it rained.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'where' to define nouns referring to place.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'where' after a place noun to define which place is meant
ontology.agency_or_distance: Spatial anchoring of an event to a specific location

positives: The city where I live is nice.
We went to the area where I used to live.
negatives: I know where you live.
This is where we met.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'when' to define nouns relating to time.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'when' after a time noun to define exactly which time is being discussed
ontology.agency_or_distance: Temporal anchoring of an event to a specific time reference

positives: I remember the day when he went back.
I was there at the time when they made it.
negatives: I know when he arrived.
When I saw him, he was sad.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'who' as the object.

ontology.mental_model: Adding non-essential information about a person
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using non-defining relative clauses with 'who' as the object to add extra details
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance from core identifying features by adding supplementary description

positives: It was Tom, who she hadn't seen for ages.
My brother, who I love, is nice.
negatives: My brother, who lives here, is nice.
The man who I saw was tall.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'why' after 'reason', to give an explanation and for focus.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the reason why' to focus on the cause of a situation
ontology.agency_or_distance: Asserting the causal link as the focal point of the sentence

positives: The reason why I love it is this.
This is the reason why we are changing it.
negatives: I don't know why he did it.
There is no reason to do that.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'who' or 'that' as the object.

ontology.mental_model: Defining a person by the actions of another subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' or 'that' as the object of a defining relative clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Specifying identity based on interaction with a distinct subject

positives: My friends are the people who I love most.
It was Sarah, a girl who I met in Spain.
negatives: My brother, who I love, is tall.
The man who is standing there is my dad.

can_do_statement: Can use defining and non-defining relative clauses with 'whose name'.

ontology.mental_model: Linking an entity to its specific identifying label
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'whose name' to provide the exact name of a person or thing
ontology.agency_or_distance: Direct nominal identification attached to a reference

positives: We have a new employee whose name is Mary.
He has a friend whose name is Robert.
negatives: I don't know whose book this is.
Whose name was called?

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions ('even though, (al)though, while if') to introduce contrast, before or after a main clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'even though' or 'although' to introduce an unexpected contrast to the main clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Navigating contradictory facts by explicitly marking contrast

positives: Although he was famous, I didn't like him.
Though we are not studying there, we keep in touch.
negatives: He is famous though.
I will see if he is there.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions to introduce reasons, after a main clause.

ontology.mental_model: Establishing a causal relationship between events
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Giving reasons with 'as' or 'since'

positives: I prefer to stay home, as I have got another appointment.
We will have to cancel the trip since it is raining heavily.
negatives: I have been living here since 2010.
She works as a manager in the new company.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions ('so (that), in order that') to introduce purpose and result, after a main clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Purpose clauses with so that / in order that

positives: Please give me some extra exercises so that I can cover the work.
Bring your camera in order that we can take photos.
negatives: I was so tired that I fell asleep immediately.
He ordered that the doors be closed.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-finite subordinate clause with 'before' and 'after' + '-ing', before or after a main clause, to refer to time.

ontology.mental_model: Linking an action in time to a progressive action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Before/After + -ing

positives: I read them in the evening before going to bed.
We can relax after working hard at school.
negatives: I saw him before the morning meeting.
She arrived after the moving truck.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE + MODAL, FUTURE, POSSIBLE OUTCOME
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple to introduce a possible future condition, with modal verbs in the main clause, to talk about a possible result. ► modality

ontology.mental_model: Setting a condition for a possible future outcome.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: First conditional with modals.

positives: I think that it would be very good if you start going to the gym.
If you come to Brazil you can stay at my home.
negatives: If he came, I would be happy.
I wonder if she knows.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT SIMPLE 'IF' CLAUSE + 'WILL', FUTURE, LIKELY OUTCOME (FIRST CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present simple to introduce a possible future condition, with 'will' in the main clause to talk about a likely result.

ontology.mental_model: Predicting a future outcome based on a condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: First conditional with 'will'.

positives: I'm sure your parents will be happy if you go with them.
If you live in the countryside you will see beautiful nature.
negatives: If you went, you would see.
If you like it, buy it.

guideword: FORM/USE: PRESENT CONTINUOUS 'IF' CLAUSE , PLANS & ADVICE
can_do_statement: Can use 'if' + present continuous or 'going to' to introduce a possible plan, with modal verbs or imperatives in the main clause to give advice.

ontology.mental_model: Conditioning advice on an ongoing plan.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'If' + present continuous for plans.

positives: Billy, if you are moving you should think a lot.
But if you are going to live in a town you should choose the large school.
negatives: If you go, call me.
If you are happy, I am happy.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST SIMPLE + 'WOULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION|(SECOND CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past simple, and would in the main clause, to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.

ontology.mental_model: Imagining a hypothetical situation to offer advice.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Second conditional ('if' + past, 'would').

positives: Maybe it would be more fun if you went with your friends.
But, if I was able to move, I would like to live near the coast.
negatives: If you go, I will be happy.
If I am late, wait for me.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST PERFECT + 'WOULD HAVE' + '-ED', IMAGINED SITUATION, REGRET|(THIRD CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past perfect simple and 'would have' + '-ed' in the main clause, to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'if' with past perfect and 'would have' to talk about imagined pasts.

positives: If they had not been there, I would have been lonely.
If I hadn't gone, I wouldn't have met her.
negatives: If I go there, I will lose my watch.
I would have been happy.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST SIMPLE + 'COULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past simple, and 'could' in the main clause to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of suggesting.

ontology.mental_model: Suggesting hypothetical possibilities for the future.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'if' with past simple and 'could' for suggestions.

positives: If you wanted to do some outdoor activities, we could go fishing.
If you arrived in town the day before, we could arrange accommodation for you.
negatives: If you want to do activities, we can go fishing.
We could go fishing today.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF I WERE YOU' + 'WOULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION
can_do_statement: Can use 'if I were you' and 'would' in the main clause often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.

ontology.mental_model: Giving advice by putting oneself in another's position.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'if I were you, I would...' to give advice.

positives: If I were you, I would accept both of them.
If I were you, I'd go to work on foot.
negatives: If I was you, I might go to work.
I would accept both of them.

can_do_statement: Can use 'unless' + present simple to talk about an exception, with present and future reference.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing exceptions to a general statement.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'unless' to talk about exceptions.

positives: I think I am going to pay by cash, unless you accept credit cards.
Unless you do some sports activities you will gain a lot of weight.
negatives: I will pay by cash if you don't accept credit cards.
He did not go to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use 'If not' as a conditional clause to offer an alternative to refer to a previous direct or indirect 'yes-no' question where the answer might be ‘no’.

ontology.mental_model: Providing an alternative to a negative condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'If not' to mean 'if the answer is no'.

positives: Is the Sheraton Hotel ok for you? If not, call me as soon as possible.
Do you work on Sundays? If not, you could do exercise on Sundays.
negatives: If he does not work, call me.
I will go if not raining.

can_do_statement: Can use 'If so' as a conditional clause to refer a previous direct or indirect 'yes-no' question where the answer might be ‘yes’. ► Clauses coordinated

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'If so' to mean 'if the answer is yes'.

positives: Do you think we could have an extra class? If so, I'd like to do it.
Is it possible to pay by credit card? If so, which ones do you take?
negatives: If it is so, we should go.
I don't know if so many people will come.

can_do_statement: Can use 'either … or' to connect two words, phrases or clauses.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an exclusive choice between two alternatives.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'either' to introduce a choice, and 'or' for the second option.

positives: You can have either cake or ice cream.
We will either walk or take the bus.
negatives: I don't like it either.
Did you see him or her?

can_do_statement: Can use 'plus' to connect clauses and sentences, often to point out a positive addition or advantage.

ontology.mental_model: Adding a positive or advantageous clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a clause with 'plus' to add a bonus point or extra reason.

positives: It's a great hotel. Plus, it's very cheap.
We have lots of food, plus we ordered pizza.
negatives: Two plus two equals four.
The total is fifty plus tax.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of conjunctions ('and, but, or, so, then') to combine more complex strings of clauses and sentences.

ontology.mental_model: Stringing multiple clauses together to narrate complex sequences.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a variety of linkers to tell a continuous, multi-step story.

positives: I was tired so I went to bed, but I couldn't sleep.
He stood up and left the room, then the phone rang.
negatives: The cat and the dog.
Either yes or no.

can_do_statement: Can use 'plus' as coordinating conjunction, often in relation to numbers.

ontology.mental_model: Adding supplementary numerical or nominal entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'plus' to add an extra item or cost to a list.

positives: It costs five dollars plus tax.
My parents will come, plus my two brothers.
negatives: Plus, I don't really want to go.
It is a big advantage, plus it saves time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'both … and' to combine noun phrases, to give emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the inclusion of two distinct nominal entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'both...and' to highlight that two things are equally involved.

positives: Both my mother and my father are doctors.
I have visited both Paris and London.
negatives: Both of them are coming.
I like apples and bananas.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of simple subordinating conjunctions ('as, after, before since, until, although, whether, so (that), though') to introduce a subordinate clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: simple subordinating conjunctions

positives: I haven't seen him since we were at school.
But I didn't remember my ring until I got back home.
negatives: I have been here since.
He did it as well.

can_do_statement: Can use no article before an increasing range of nouns in some fixed expressions with prepositions.

ontology.mental_model: Expanded prepositional expressions for abstract entities and conditions.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Broader use of prepositions without articles for conditions and broad concepts.

positives: It gets quite cold at night.
I saw the documentary on television.
negatives: We had a long night.
Please turn on the television.

can_do_statement: Can use 'another' to talk about something additional.

ontology.mental_model: Additionality mapped onto an existing set.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'another' to mean 'one more' of the same kind.

positives: I am going to spend another week there.
Can I have another slice of pizza?
negatives: He told me another story altogether.
Let's meet at another place.

can_do_statement: Can use no article before an increasing range of singular and plural nouns when referring to things in general.

ontology.mental_model: Broader generalization across domains like society or nature.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Zero article used for abstract, overarching concepts.

positives: Education is very important for our future.
History will show that we were right.
negatives: The education he received was excellent.
A love like theirs is rare.

can_do_statement: Can use 'another' with singular nouns. ► pronouns ► determiners

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'another' to refer to a single extra item or instance.

positives: Tomorrow will be another day.
He makes another great joke.
negatives: We need another two weeks.
Let's meet another time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'another' to talk about something different.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'Another' can also mean 'a different one'.

positives: It is better to stay at another hotel.
We should go to another restaurant.
negatives: Have another slice of cake.
I will wait another minute.

can_do_statement: Can use 'the other' with a singular noun to refer to the second or the opposite of two things, and with a plural noun to refer to one of a set of things. ► pronouns ►  noun phrases

ontology.mental_model: Binary distinction or definite selection from a set.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'The other' refers to the remaining option out of two or a known group.

positives: I moved because the other house was too small.
I saw him on the other side of the street.
negatives: I have other plans.
Some people like it, others don't.

can_do_statement: Can use 'this' with time and date words to refer to the past.

ontology.mental_model: Identification of past temporal points or periods.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Referring to 'this' past event or time.

positives: I received your letter this morning.
It happened this summer.
negatives: I will receive your letter tomorrow morning.
It will happen next summer.

can_do_statement: Can use ''s' after irregular plural nouns to indicate possession.

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: They attract people's attention.
It is far from the children's school.
negatives: The people are waiting.
The dog's bone is buried here.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiner 'their'. ► noun phrases ► possessive pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Mapping possession, quantification, or specific reference to an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Identifying the scope or owner of a noun phrase.

positives: They returned to their car.
I couldn't see their faces.
negatives: There is a problem.
They are coming over.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('half of', 'enough of', 'none of',).► pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'half of', 'enough of', or 'none of' followed by 'the' or 'my'.

positives: You should spend half of your holiday with parents.
None of the stores had it.
negatives: You should spend half a holiday.
No stores had it.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns ('most', 'enough', 'plenty of', 'loads of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing sufficiency, majority, or abundance for countable and uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'most', 'enough', 'plenty of', or 'loads of'.

positives: I am convinced that most people watch TV.
We will have plenty of time to buy tickets.
negatives: I am convinced that many people watch TV.
We will have a lot of time to buy tickets.

guideword: FORM: 'SO MUCH', 'TOO MUCH' WITH UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use 'so much' and 'too much' with uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so much' or 'too much' to exaggerate a lot of something.

positives: I have so much work at the moment.
My neighbours are making too much noise.
negatives: I have a lot of work.
My neighbours are making too many noises.

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'much' with uncountable things.

positives: How much television do you watch?
Do you have much time left?
negatives: I don't watch much television.
How many televisions do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use quantifying determiners with uncountable nouns, often in informal and/or spoken contexts ('a little', 'a bit of' and 'a little bit of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing a small, indefinite quantity of uncountable entities in informal contexts.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a little', 'a bit of', or 'a little bit of'.

positives: We could spend a little time together.
I just watch a little bit of TV.
negatives: We could spend some time together.
I watch a lot of TV.

can_do_statement: Can use 'many' with plural nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'many' with plural things.

positives: Have you got many friends in England?
How many channels are there in Britain?
negatives: I don't have many friends.
How much money do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('several', 'millions of', 'a few of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing larger or diverse quantities of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'several', 'millions of', or 'a few of'.

positives: Several days ago we received a complaint.
They interviewed a few of the students.
negatives: Many days ago we received a complaint.
They interviewed some students.

can_do_statement: Can modify determiners with adverbs. ► adverbs

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'almost all' or 'nearly every'.

positives: Because almost all of the programmes are stupid.
We've spent nearly every day together.
negatives: I have almost finished my homework.
She is just arriving.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of words and phrases as discourse markers to add information.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring discourse by explicitly adding to previous points.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'moreover' or 'furthermore' to add ideas.

positives: Moreover the health of our staff is essential.
Furthermore, I think that you should exercise.
negatives: I want to learn more.
We will go further into the forest.

guideword: FORM/USE: ORGANISING, MARKING NEW KNOWLEDGE, INFORMAL
can_do_statement: Can use 'you see', 'the thing is' as discourse markers to mark new knowledge, usually in informal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Introducing explanatory or new information conversationally.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'you see' or 'the thing is' to explain.

positives: You see, in the park, you can enjoy fresh air.
The thing is, I'd go to the countryside.
negatives: I see what you mean.
The thing is very heavy.

can_do_statement: Can use sequencing adverbs as discourse markers to organise text.

ontology.mental_model: Structuring discourse logically using ordinal adverbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'firstly', 'secondly', 'finally'.

positives: Firstly, we need a good expert.
Secondly, good materials are needed.
negatives: He came first in the race.
It was my last chance.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of phrases as discourse markers to introduce contrasting statements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'on the other hand' or 'on the contrary'.

positives: On the other hand I think you can learn better.
My new teacher, on the contrary, understands us.
negatives: I hurt my other hand.
The contrary is true.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs as discourse markers to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing speaker attitude or evaluation of a proposition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using stance adverbs like 'unfortunately' or 'actually'.

positives: Unfortunately, they filmed only the building.
Actually, I do not have much time.
negatives: He is an honest man.
It is an actual fact.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs in the front position for focus.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting the spotlight on the adverb

positives: Suddenly, the door swung wide open.
Quickly I grabbed my coat and left.
negatives: The door suddenly swung wide open.
I quickly grabbed my coat and left.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it' + 'be' + adjective + 'that-'clause for focus.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Stating an opinion objectively

positives: It's great that you found a new apartment.
It is important that everyone arrives on time.
negatives: I think that it is a great idea.
That book is really great.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will' and 'shall'.

ontology.mental_model: Visualizing an action in progress at a point in the future using formal auxiliary
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'shall be -ing' or 'will be -ing' for future ongoing actions.

positives: I shall be attending class the day after tomorrow.
We will be waiting for you at the cafe.
negatives: I shall go to the market later.
I will be happy to assist you.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'will' ('won’t').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing that an action will not be in progress at a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'won't be -ing' to say what you will not be doing in the future.

positives: I won't be attending your English class next week.
He will not be coming to the party.
negatives: I will be attending the class.
I won't go there.

can_do_statement: Can use the simple past form of 'be' + 'going to' to talk about the future from a point in the past. ► 'be going to'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing what was planned in the past but usually didn't happen

positives: She was going to return it but she saw something very strange.
We were clearly going to meet two days later in the square.
negatives: I am going to do it tomorrow.
She was going to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to talk about the future from a point in the past.► 'would'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: expressing future outcomes as seen from a past moment

positives: I knew it would be a lovely birthday present.
We thought that the film would be horrible.
negatives: I would like to have a coffee.
If I had money, I would buy a car.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall' with 'I' and 'we' to talk about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'shall' as an alternative to 'will' for describing personal plans.

positives: I promise that I shall cover all the work tomorrow.
We shall have a meeting regarding this next week.
negatives: Shall we go out?
He shall do it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' and '‘ll' to make predictions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' to state what one believes will happen.

positives: It will be hotter because of global warming.
They will not worry about you too much!
negatives: I will definitely go there.
We'll see what happens.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to talk about fixed plans, often with timetabled times and dates.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' in conjunction with times and dates for fixed events.

positives: The work will start at eight.
I won't be able at the time we agreed.
negatives: I will do it later.
It will rain tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I am not going to go to school tomorrow.
There is not going to be an adult there.
negatives: I am not going to the store.
She isn't going to the park.

can_do_statement: Can use the past form of 'be' + 'going to'. ► future in the past

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: It was going to be an extremely hot day.
We were going to meet at 11.30 am.
negatives: I was going to the hospital.
They were going to their hometown.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be' + 'going to' with a limited range of adverbs, after the auxiliary be form, in the normal mid position.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I'm never going to forget this moment.
We are really going to miss you.
negatives: I am going to learn it.
She is currently going to the market.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form of 'be going to' to talk about plans and intentions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I'm not going to be able to meet you.
I am sure I am not going to live there forever.
negatives: They are not going to the event.
He isn't going to school today.

can_do_statement: Can use the past form of 'be going to' to refer to the future from a point in the past. ► future in the past

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: She didn't know what was going to happen.
We were going to meet two days later.
negatives: I was going to the supermarket.
They were going to London.

can_do_statement: Can use the past form of 'be going to' as the reported form.► reported speech

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: He told me he was going to arrive tomorrow.
I thought it was going to rain.
negatives: I was going to call you.
She thought he went to the market.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be going to' with an increasing range of verbs to make predictions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using future constructs to indicate forthcoming actions or states.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency via intention; Distance via forward-looking temporal projection.

positives: I think you're going to like it.
I think I am going to enjoy that class.
negatives: He is going to the hospital.
I am going to the market.

can_do_statement: Can use the past form of 'be going to' (often followed by 'but') to talk about a plan, sometimes one that may have changed.

ontology.mental_model: past intention that may have been altered
ontology.pedagogical_hook: past plans using 'was/were going to'

positives: We were going to have a cup of coffee on Tuesday.
I was really going to call you, but I forgot.
negatives: We are going to get married.
I was going to the shop when I saw him.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with an increasing range of verbs to talk about future arrangements.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: present continuous for arrangements (B1)

positives: I am attending a funeral tomorrow.
The movie is starting very soon.
negatives: I attend meetings every day.
Are you attending the funeral tomorrow?

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous with an increasing range of verbs to ask about future plans.

ontology.mental_model: inquiry about fixed arrangement in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: present continuous for future questions (B1)

positives: Are you visiting my country on your next holiday?
Why are you moving to a different area?
negatives: Do you expect a call?
I am visiting my country on holiday.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple with 'as soon as' to refer to the future.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: present simple with 'as soon as'

positives: I'm planning to move as soon as I finish college.
I will let you know as soon as the date approaches.
negatives: I left as soon as I arrived.
Please reply as soon as possible.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it' + 'be' + 'important' + ('that') clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'it is important that' clause

positives: It's important that you take breaks.
It is important that the children sleep well.
negatives: It is important to listen.
An important thing is that you listen.

can_do_statement: Can use 'if-' clauses + 'possible', as a politeness strategy.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Softening requests with conditional possibility

positives: If it is possible I would like to pay by credit card.
If possible, could you please send it again?
negatives: It is possible if you try hard enough.
I wonder if a possible solution exists.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it' + 'be' + adjective + 'to' + infinitive, to make an assertion more or less direct.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Presenting evaluations objectively

positives: Sometimes it is essential to do what they want.
It was absolutely impossible to install the system.
negatives: It is possible that he will arrive late.
The task is impossible to finish.

can_do_statement: Can use 'it' + 'be' + adjective + 'for' + object + 'to' + infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: Impersonal requirement directed at a specific entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Stating requirements for someone else

positives: It is important for you to know what they are like.
It is essential for me to go now.
negatives: It is important to know the rules.
For me, it is essential.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative question forms in main clauses and question tags.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker combines a question and negation into a single modal structure for emphasis or tag requests.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'can't' at the start of a question or at the end as a tag to ask for confirmation.

positives: Can't you go with your parents?
You can ask your parents, can't you?
negatives: I can't go with you.
She cannot come today.

can_do_statement: Can use 'can' with a limited range of adverbs (including 'also', 'always', 'even', 'just', 'only', 'really', 'still') in the normal mid position after the modal verb.   ► adverbs

ontology.mental_model: Speaker modifies the intensity or scope of 'can' using specific adverbs placed immediately after the modal.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Put adverbs like 'also', 'just', or 'only' immediately after 'can' to add extra meaning.

positives: You can also write postcards.
I can't even remember the face.
negatives: I can never remember.
I really can't say.

can_do_statement: Can use 'can be' to talk about general truths and tendencies.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker evaluates typical states or conditions using 'can be' with non-personal subjects.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use 'can be' to talk about what is generally true or common in certain situations.

positives: The centre of town can be dangerous.
Summer can be very boring.
negatives: I can be there tomorrow.
You can be whatever you want.

can_do_statement: Can use 'can you believe' to express surprise.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker conveys disbelief or amazement using the rhetorical phrase 'can you believe'.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use the phrase 'can you believe' to show that you are very surprised by something.

positives: They invented a robot, can you believe this?
Can you believe that!
negatives: I can believe it.
Do you believe me?

can_do_statement: Can use a range of modal verbs + 'be able to' + infinitive.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Guessing about ability

positives: We might be able to fix the car ourselves.
You should be able to see the mountain from here.
negatives: I will be able to do it later.
He is able to run fast.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be allowed to' to talk about permission.

ontology.mental_model: Authorization and permission granted by external authority
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Talking about rules

positives: She isn't allowed to stay out late.
We were allowed to enter the building.
negatives: I allowed him to go.
They are allowing us to stay.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of expressions with 'be' + infinitive ('be allowed to', 'be supposed to', 'be able to') with present and past forms of 'be' and with modal 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: Core modality using 'be' for capability, expectation, and permission
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic modal phrases with 'be'

positives: I am supposed to finish my homework.
They are not able to see the stage.
negatives: They supposed it was true.
She allowed the dog inside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'was supposed to', 'were supposed to' to refer to past or future arrangements which may not have happened or may change.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Talking about failed plans

positives: We were supposed to go yesterday.
I was supposed to tell you about the change.
negatives: I am supposed to go tomorrow.
They supposed it was a joke.

can_do_statement: Can use 'was able to', 'were able to' to talk about facts in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Past capability leading to a factual outcome
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Talking about past achievements

positives: I was able to find my lost keys.
They weren't able to complete the test.
negatives: I am able to speak three languages.
She will be able to join us later.

can_do_statement: Can use the fixed expression 'I have to admit' for emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: fixed phrase for emphasis and concession
ontology.pedagogical_hook: I have to admit

positives: I have to admit that it was a good movie.
I've to admit I was wrong.
negatives: She has to admit her mistakes.
I have to leave now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'have to' as an infinitive form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: to have to

positives: I am going to have to buy a new one.
I'd hate to have to choose between them.
negatives: I have to go.
She wants to have a break.

can_do_statement: Can use 'may' with a limited range of adverbs (most commonly 'also') in the normal mid-position after the modal verb. ► adverbs

ontology.pedagogical_hook: may also

positives: It may also help you relax.
I may probably come.
negatives: I may go to the park.
May I also ask?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: may not

positives: I knew I may not meet him.
It may not be the best way.
negatives: I may go later.
May I ask a question?

can_do_statement: Can use 'may I' to ask for permission.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: May I for permission

positives: May I borrow your bike?
May I be your guide today?
negatives: I may need to borrow this.
He may have gone.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might' to make polite suggestions and give advice.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To give gentle advice or suggest an idea politely, tell someone 'you might' do something.

positives: You might need to bring some food and drink.
I think that you might talk with your parents.
negatives: He might talk to his parents.
You might be late.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might have' + '-ed' to talk about possibility with a past reference.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To talk about what was possible in the past, use 'might have' with the past participle.

positives: Many things might have led to these changes.
I thought that a burglar might have broken into our house.
negatives: He might have a lot of money.
She might have to leave early.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might have' + '-ed'.

ontology.mental_model: Forming the past modal of possibility
ontology.pedagogical_hook: To make 'might' past tense, add 'have' and a past participle.

positives: It might have been our neighbours' cat.
He might have seen us.
negatives: They might have some issues.
I might have to go now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might' as the past form of 'may' in indirect reports.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: When reporting what someone said using 'may', change it to 'might'.

positives: My parents said it might be the last holiday.
Lisa thought it might be a lucky one so she showed it to her Dad.
negatives: It might rain today.
They say it might snow tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To say it's possible something won't happen, use 'might not' or 'mightn't'.

positives: It might not be very fashionable.
This mightn't be such a good thing.
negatives: It might be a problem.
She might go to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use 'might' in phrases, such as 'as you might know', 'have already heard', to focus the reader on shared knowledge.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Shared knowledge focus

positives: As you might know, we are moving.
As you might have heard, she resigned.
negatives: You might know the answer to this.
They might have heard the news by now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' to make invitations.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Strong invitations

positives: You must come and stay with us.
You must try this cake!
negatives: He must come to work on time.
I must try harder.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' with a limited range of adverbs (most commonly 'also') in the normal mid position after the modal verb. ► adverbs

ontology.mental_model: Using adverbs like also or always with must
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Adverbs with must

positives: You must also bring your book.
He must always be early.
negatives: You must bring your book also.
Always you must be early.

can_do_statement: Can use ellipted 'must' without a subject. ► ellipsis

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Subject ellipsis

positives: Must go now, bye!
Must be difficult for him.
negatives: I must go now, bye!
It must be difficult for him.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' with the following verb ellipted where the previous main verb is understood.    ► ellipsis

ontology.mental_model: Dropping the main verb after must
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Verb ellipsis

positives: Because I must!
If you really must, then go.
negatives: I must go!
You must see it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' to guess and deduce, most commonly with 'it must be', or 'you must be'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Speculating on situations

positives: It must be boring for you to sit at a computer all day.
You must really be so nervous.
negatives: They must be at work by now.
We must be careful when crossing the street.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' (with a wide range of pronouns and nouns) to talk about obligation and necessity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Expressing obligations

positives: We must go and find him.
Your parents must absolutely learn to let you live your own life.
negatives: He must be very tired after the long journey.
It must seem like a crazy idea.

can_do_statement: Can use 'must' to make strong, encouraging suggestions.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Recommending activities

positives: I mean we must clearly see it.
Rome is fantastic and you must visit there!
negatives: They must try to repair the car.
She must go to the doctor right away.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Basic structure of 'ought to' plus verb

positives: I think we ought to leave now.
She ought to definitely call her mother.
negatives: She ought to have called.
I bought a car to drive.

can_do_statement: Can use 'ought to' with 'you' to give advice.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'you ought to' for advice

positives: You ought to talk to your parents first.
I think you really ought to play tennis.
negatives: He ought to play tennis.
You should talk to your parents.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall' to talk about plans and intentions, particularly in formal contexts.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'shall' instead of 'will' to state what one intends to do.

positives: I shall cover all the work.
We shall be attending the event.
negatives: Shall we go?
The law shall cover that.

can_do_statement: Can use 'shall' to seek advice.

ontology.mental_model: Asking for guidance on the best course of action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: 'What/where/how shall I/we' for advice.

positives: What shall I do?
Where shall we go?
negatives: Shall we dance?
I shall do my best.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should have' + '-ed'.

ontology.mental_model: An action was not recommended or required in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When did you do something you weren't supposed to? Say 'I shouldn't have done it'.

positives: I know I shouldn't have taken it during school time.
She really should not have gone there alone.
negatives: I shouldn't have any problems.
You should have been with us.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should' have + '-ed'.

ontology.mental_model: An action was recommended or required in the past, but likely didn't happen.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When did you miss out on something? Say 'I should have gone'.

positives: You should have been with us.
I knew I should have written before.
negatives: I shouldn't have taken it.
You should have a good time.

can_do_statement: Can use the question tag form 'shouldn't' + pronoun to make suggestions and ask for opinions.

ontology.mental_model: Seeking confirmation for a proposed action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Make a suggestion and ask if it's right using ', shouldn't we?'

positives: We should rent some movies, shouldn't we?
I should write about the history, shouldn't I?
negatives: You shouldn't do that.
Shouldn't it be here by now?

can_do_statement: Can use 'should' to talk about what is likely to happen.

ontology.mental_model: Predicting a probable outcome based on current conditions.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: What is likely to happen? Say 'It should be fine'.

positives: It should be a good day!
The weather should be nice tomorrow.
negatives: You should eat more vegetables.
I should have written before.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should' to talk about ideal or desired situations.

ontology.mental_model: Describing how the world ought to be, universally.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: What would make the world better? Say 'People should...'

positives: British people should eat more vegetables.
I think everyone should learn to cook.
negatives: You should bring your guitar.
It should be a good day!

can_do_statement: Can use 'you shouldn’t have' (+ '-ed') in polite acceptance of a gift.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing gratitude by playfully suggesting a gift was unnecessary.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Receive a gift? Say 'Thank you, you shouldn't have!'

positives: Thank you for the present you sent me, you shouldn't have!
Thanks for the money, you shouldn't have sent it.
negatives: You shouldn't have done that.
I shouldn't have taken it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'you should have' + '-ed' to emphasise points in a story.

ontology.mental_model: Highlighting the extreme nature of a past event to a listener.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Telling a crazy story? Say 'You should have seen...'

positives: You should have heard the noise.
You should have seen my face, I was so happy.
negatives: I should have written before.
You should have eaten your vegetables.

can_do_statement: Can use 'should have' + '-ed' to talk about regrets or undesirable situations in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing sorrow over a past action that cannot be changed.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Regret something? Say 'I'm sorry, I shouldn't have done it'.

positives: He had written that he was sorry and that he should not have done it.
Unfortunately, I should have studied more for the exam.
negatives: You should have been there with me, I had a great time.
You should have seen my face!

can_do_statement: Can use 'used to' to talk about repeated actions or states in the past that are no longer true.

ontology.mental_model: Past habit or state now discontinued
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past habits that stopped

positives: I used to live in London.
She used to be a teacher.
negatives: I am used to living in London.
This tool is used to open bottles.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Affirmative past habits

positives: I used to share my room with my brother.
We used to be together all the time.
negatives: I didn't use to laugh much.
Did you use to go there?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms 'didn't use to' and 'didn't used to'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negative past habits

positives: We didn't use to talk to each other.
I didn't used to go there.
negatives: What did we use to eat?
I used to talk to him.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to talk about fixed plans in the future, often with timetabled times or dates.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'will' to discuss scheduled future events

positives: I will see you tomorrow at noon.
We'll arrive next Thursday morning.
negatives: I will definitely do it for you.
He visited us next to the bank.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' to make predictions.► question tags

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Making predictions and confirming with question tags

positives: You'll soon put on weight, won't you?
It will be much harder, won't it?
negatives: You didn't do it, did you?
I will go to the market tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would not have' + '-ed' or 'wouldn’t have' + '-ed'

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would not have [past participle]'

positives: I wouldn't have got this result without you.
She would not have met George otherwise.
negatives: I would have done it.
She wouldn't have any money left.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would have' + '-ed'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would have [past participle]'

positives: I did not think my friend Janis would have done that.
That answer would have changed my life.
negatives: I wouldn't have done that.
I would have a nice car by now.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' in the main clause of a conditional sentence to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.

ontology.mental_model: Speculating about imagined scenarios, especially for advice.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would' in conditional main clauses to give advice.

positives: If I were you, I would not watch TV all the time.
If I had the chance, I'd go with my friends.
negatives: I would like a cup of tea.
She said she would arrive late.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to talk about the future in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Referring to an event that was in the future from a past perspective.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would' as the past form of 'will' to talk about the future from the past.

positives: I thought they would be great for the party.
We believed the film would be horrible.
negatives: I think they will be great.
I would like to go there.

can_do_statement: Can use an limited range of adverbs with 'would', including 'really', 'probably', 'certainly', 'definitely'.► adverbs

ontology.mental_model: Modifying the degree of certainty or emphasis of 'would'.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using adverbs like 'really', 'probably', 'certainly' with 'would'.

positives: I think you would really enjoy it.
It would probably be the best idea.
negatives: I really like it.
She would like to definitely go.

can_do_statement: Can use question forms.

ontology.mental_model: Forming questions using 'would' to ask for opinions or offer.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Inverting 'would' and subject to ask a question.

positives: Would you let me know what you think?
Wouldn't that be wonderful?
negatives: I wouldn't do that.
You would let me know.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to make polite requests, often in the fixed expression 'would you mind'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would you mind' or similar polite structures.

positives: Would you mind if we met at five?
Would it be possible for you to meet me?
negatives: I would mind if you did that.
It would be possible.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' with verbs such as 'advise', 'imagine', 'recommend', 'say' to be less direct.

ontology.mental_model: Using 'would' to soften statements and sound less direct.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would advise', 'would say' to be less direct.

positives: I'd advise you to go with your friends.
Finally, I'd say that you should talk with your parents.
negatives: I advise you to do it.
She said she would go.

guideword: USE: IMAGINED SITUATIONS IN THE PAST
can_do_statement: Can use 'would' to talk about imagined situations in the past. ► conditionals

ontology.mental_model: Speculating about imagined scenarios in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would have' to talk about imagined situations in the past.

positives: The next week I would have flown to Miami.
I wouldn't have known how to do it.
negatives: I would have a coffee.
I have known him for years.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would' as the past form of 'will' in reported clauses.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would' as the past form of 'will' in reported speech.

positives: She said that she would come.
He told me I would like it.
negatives: She said that she wants to come.
I would like to tell you.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms of 'would' to talk about willingness in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing refusal or unwillingness in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'would not' or 'wouldn't' to show past unwillingness.

positives: The bus driver wouldn't wait.
My parents would not allow me to buy it.
negatives: I wouldn't go there.
I would wait for you.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs, for emphasis.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using varied adverbs to emphasize claims

positives: I'd certainly choose not to go with your parents.
You obviously can't keep fit.
negatives: Maybe I will go.
Perhaps it is true.

guideword: FORM/USE: MODAL VERB + MODAL ADVERB, HEDGING OR EMPHASIS
can_do_statement: Can use modal verb + modal adverb to modify an assertion, either through hedging or emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker evaluates probability or necessity using a modal verb combined with a modifying adverb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: We use adverbs like 'probably', 'certainly', or 'surely' after modal verbs to emphasize or hedge the meaning.

positives: You should probably bring your coat.
He could definitely win the race.
negatives: He probably should bring his coat.
You definitely have a point.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' + subject + 'possibly' to make requests more polite.

ontology.mental_model: Speaker softens a request by adding 'possibly' to make it extremely polite.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'Could you possibly...?' when asking for a big favor.

positives: Could you possibly help me with this?
Could we possibly change the time?
negatives: You could possibly win the game.
Could you help me?

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form of 'could' to talk about ability.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'could' with ability verbs

positives: She could hear a man talking.
I could run very fast when I was younger.
negatives: We could go out for dinner.
You could try the other door.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could I' to seek permission.

ontology.mental_model: Agent shifts focus to themselves with 'could I' to ask for authorization or permission.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking for permission politely

positives: Could I take the class that I will miss on Saturday?
Could I play with it now, please?
negatives: I could run very fast when I was a kid.
We could meet later.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' to talk about possibility.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' with abstract subjects (it, this) to assess likelihood or potential truth.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying something might be true
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: stepping back to evaluate probability

positives: it could be really fun to have a talkative person
Could this really happen?
negatives: Could you pass the salt?
We could have dinner after that.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' with an increasing range of verbs to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' to propose varied actions as possibilities for the listener.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Suggesting actions with more variety
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: offering a broader array of choices

positives: We could meet in the nice cafe next to your house.
you could become a member of a gym.
negatives: I could jump really high back then.
Could I get a glass of water?

can_do_statement: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the past continuous and past perfect with auxiliary verbs 'be' and 'have' + 'not/n't'. ► past continuous ► past perfect

ontology.mental_model: Absence of an ongoing or preceding past event
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Negating past continuous and past perfect with 'not'.

positives: It was raining for seventy two hours and it wasn't going to stop.
I hadn't expected to receive a letter from her.
negatives: I am not expecting a letter.
She hasn't been feeling well.

can_do_statement: Can use negative question forms in main clauses and question tags. ► questions

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Starting a question with a negative auxiliary or using a negative question tag.

positives: Can't you go with your parents some time?
You're free on Saturday, aren't you?
negatives: I can't go with my parents.
She didn't think it was a good idea.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms of mental process verbs ('I don’t think', 'I don’t believe') followed by a complement clause, where the negative form is in the mental process verb rather than the complement clause.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing a negative opinion or belief
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'I don't think' instead of 'I think it is not'.

positives: But I don't think it'll help you.
I don't believe that the suitcase will be returned to me.
negatives: I didn't hear what you said.
They do not know if they can come.

guideword: FORM: 'NOT', NON FINITE AND ELLIPTED CLAUSES
can_do_statement: Can use 'not' before a non-finite or ellipted clause.

ontology.mental_model: Negating a fragment or non-finite verb
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not' alone before a participle or adjective.

positives: I ripped it open as fast as I could. Not this time.
I would like to apologise for not being able to attend.
negatives: I am not going to the store.
He did not want to see it.

can_do_statement: Can use negative questions and question tags to involve the listener/reader by seeking agreement or checking something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using negative questions or tags to involve the listener.

positives: Isn't it marvellous?
You love books, don't you?
negatives: I didn't think it was marvellous.
He doesn't love books.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns in negative contexts.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using indefinite pronouns like 'nothing' or 'anyone' in negative contexts.

positives: I said I had nothing, but he didn't believe me.
I haven't seen anything yet.
negatives: I have something for you.
Everyone is here.

can_do_statement: Can use adverbs 'ever', 'never', 'yet', 'still' in negative contexts.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using time adverbs to reinforce negation

positives: Nobody will ever know who that man was.
I haven't decided yet.
negatives: I have ever been there.
Are you still coming to the party?

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADVERBS + ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with adverb + adjective + noun.

ontology.mental_model: Intensifying or modulating the property of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using an adverb like 'very' or 'really' before an adjective that describes a noun.

positives: It took a very long time.
They made really good friends.
negatives: The time was very long.
They are really good.

can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases by using a prepositional phrase after the main noun in a noun phrase.

ontology.mental_model: Adding structural or relational details to an entity using a preposition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Following a noun with a preposition like 'with', 'about', or 'of' to give more details.

positives: It was a red dress with blue flowers.
He asked about the future of my town.
negatives: I went with him.
She spoke about the issue.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with more than one adjective.

ontology.mental_model: Providing detailed descriptions using multiple adjectives.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a sequence of descriptive words before a noun.

positives: I bought a white hooded jacket.
He had short, curly, red hair.
negatives: I bought a jacket.
The hair was short and red.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with 'such a' + adjective + singular noun and 'such' + adjective + plural noun, to give emphasis.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the degree or quality of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'such' or 'such a' before an adjective and a noun to show strong feeling.

positives: I have never been in such a terrible situation.
We were such good friends.
negatives: I am looking for such things.
It was such a pity.

can_do_statement: Can use a clause with a present perfect or past perfect as a superlative noun phrase complement, to talk about uniqueness.

ontology.mental_model: Describing an entity as the ultimate extreme within one's lifetime experience.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a superlative adjective followed by 'I have ever' or 'I had ever'.

positives: It is the best book I have ever read.
She's the funniest person I've known.
negatives: He is the tallest boy in the class.
I have seen the best movie.

can_do_statement: Can omit the noun after possessive '’s' to talk about a place which is familiar to the speaker and listener.

ontology.mental_model: Referring to a location associated with a person or entity without explicitly naming the place.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using apostrophe S ('s) at the end of a sentence or phrase without the noun it possesses.

positives: I have to go to the dentist's.
It is next to your grandma's.
negatives: It is my grandma's house.
He's coming tomorrow.

can_do_statement: Can put two noun phrases together (in apposition) to refer to the same person or thing, usually separated by commas.

ontology.mental_model: Two noun phrases side-by-side to define the same entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When you want to give more detail about a noun you just mentioned, you can add another noun phrase right after it, usually between commas.

positives: Mr Miller, the Sales Director, will visit us next Thursday.
A new employee, Mary Watts, has just joined our company.
negatives: Mr Miller will visit us next Thursday, and the Sales Director will come too.
A new employee has just joined our company, which is great.

can_do_statement: Can use the noun phrase 'The thing' in front position, with a clause complement, to give focus to something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To highlight a specific point or aspect, start your sentence with 'The thing (that)...'

positives: The thing I enjoyed most about it was a new computer game.
The thing I prefer there is the swimming-pool.
negatives: I enjoyed the thing you gave me.
I prefer the swimming-pool, that is the thing.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE '‘S' + NOUN
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with noun phrase + 'of' + noun phrase + possessive determiner ''s' + noun phrase.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: You can link two possessive ideas by using 'of' followed by a noun with an apostrophe 's'.

positives: I saw the window of my neighbour's car was broken.
The subject of my boss's talk will be IT skills.
negatives: I saw my neighbour's car was broken.
The subject of the talk will be IT skills.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with an indefinite pronoun + adjective or clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: When describing an indefinite pronoun (like something or nothing), the adjective comes after the pronoun.

positives: We see each other every day and do something different every day.
But then there is nothing special to eat.
negatives: We do different things every day.
There are no special meals to eat.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with 'a friend of' or 'friends of' + possessive determiner + noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: You can describe relationships by saying 'a friend of' followed by a possessive determiner and a noun.

positives: He is a friend of my husband.
I thought they were friends of my neighbour.
negatives: He is my husband's friend.
I thought they were my neighbour's friends.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with noun + 'of' + possessive pronouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a noun followed by 'of' and a possessive pronoun (like 'mine', 'yours', 'his') to indicate that it's one of many things belonging to someone.

positives: I told her lots of silly mistakes of mine.
I'm a fan of his, he is my favorite singer.
negatives: I told her lots of my silly mistakes.
I'm his fan, he is my favorite singer.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of common nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a wider variety of everyday common nouns.

positives: When you're swimming you exercise all of your body.
My heart was hurt and nobody will repair the damage.
negatives: I go.
She went.

can_do_statement: Can use collective nouns, usually with a singular verb, but also with a plural verb depending on whether the noun is perceived as a single group or collection of individuals.

ontology.mental_model: Singular entity consisting of multiple individuals
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Nouns that represent groups taking either singular or plural verbs.

positives: The staff is friendly.
The crew were very interested.
negatives: I joined the team.
I have a big family.

can_do_statement: Can use uncountable nouns with an increasing range of quantity words and phrases including 'much', 'a bit of', 'a little bit of', 'enough', 'further', 'plenty of', 'loads of'.  ►  Determiners: quantity

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Expressing amounts of uncountable things with phrases like 'a bit of' or 'plenty of'.

positives: I hope this little bit of advice can help you!
So I would like you to attend a meeting next week for further information.
negatives: I don't have many apples.
A few cars are here.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of uncountable nouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a broader variety of uncountable nouns, such as countryside or accommodation.

positives: I think the countryside is better than the town centre
I hope you can help me to find new accommodation as soon as is possible.
negatives: The cats are nice.
He read a book.

guideword: FORM/USE: WITH 'BY' IN A RELATIVE CLAUSE|
can_do_statement: Can use the passive with 'by' in a relative clause, often to add more information.

ontology.mental_model: Elaboration of entity through passive action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Relative clause passive agent.

positives: These are the shirts which were made by local artisans.
The man who was bitten by a dog is in the hospital.
negatives: The house was built by a famous architect.
He is the one who lives by the river.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple passive (general).

positives: The walls are painted green.
I am invited to the party.
negatives: They are not allowed inside.
She was driven home.

can_do_statement: Can use the past simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects both singular and plural.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple passive (general).

positives: The cookies were eaten by the kids.
The car was stolen last night.
negatives: The cookies were not eaten.
She is invited to dinner.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous passive affirmative with a limited range of verbs.

ontology.mental_model: Ongoing passive action in the present.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present continuous passive.

positives: The movie is being filmed right now.
The samples are being tested.
negatives: The movie was being filmed.
The movie is not being filmed.

can_do_statement: Can use the passive infinitive after a limited number of forms including 'going to', 'have to', 'need to', 'want to'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Passive infinitive after semi-modals.

positives: It needs to be washed.
The papers have to be signed.
negatives: It can be washed.
She wants to be a doctor.

can_do_statement: Can use the present continuous passive to refer to the future.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present continuous passive for future.

positives: The meeting is being held next week.
We are being audited tomorrow.
negatives: The meeting is being held right now.
We are being audited.

can_do_statement: Can use the passive with 'by' to give focus.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasising the agent in a passive construction.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Passive with 'by' for focus.

positives: The winner was chosen by the audience.
The bridge was designed by a famous architect.
negatives: I live by the river.
It is done.

guideword: FORM: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS.
can_do_statement: Can use the past simple passive with a limited range of verbs needing two objects, putting the indirect object in subject position.

ontology.mental_model: Focus on the recipient rather than the actor
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple passive with two objects

positives: I was given a second chance by my manager.
They were offered a free meal after the mistake.
negatives: I have been given a lot of homework.
She gave him a ticket for the train.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple passive negative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing negative state or action received by subject in present
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present simple passive negative

positives: The documents are not printed in color.
